paragraphs.text: "While men slept": the sleep of those responsible for the planting, that is, the priests and servants, and it means the lack of spiritual vigilance and care for the people.

The enemy: he is Satan, and he is not an enemy of the husbandmen or the wheat, but of God and all His children. He took advantage of the opportunity of the sleep of the husbandmen responsible for the field, and sowed the seeds of tares, which point to the heresies that the originators of innovations plant in the hearts of some people, and so turn them away from God. Or they signify sins and lusts that defile people, so that they become wicked and do not give the good fruit that God was awaiting from them. "Tares": seeds similar to the seeds of wheat, but they are weeds that harm the original plant, that is, the wheat. "Wheat": grain.

"Went his way": in secret, as if he had done nothing, although he is the cause of the evil in the world. My beloved brother... how necessary it is for each of us to be spiritually alert, so as not to accept evil thoughts or lusts that turn us away from God, and if he is a servant, to care for those he serves, lest they turn into tares and be turned away from God.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: When the seeds grew, the tare plants appeared, that is, foreign weeds, different from the wheat... "by their fruits ye shall know them"; the wheat gave ears, but the tares at the beginning are similar to wheat as a little plant, but when they grew, the known ears of wheat did not appear on them... So the works of the children of God are good, and the works of the wicked are evil.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: "The servants of the householder": they are the spiritual servants, whether bishops or priests or everyone who serves in the Church, and they noticed that there are wicked people in the world far from God, because their fruits differ from the beloved ears of wheat, and they were greatly astonished at this change, for they had expected good fruits from all the plants, because all God's planting is good.

And when they inquired about the reason for the presence of the tares, the householder informed them that an enemy, that is, Satan, had done this, and put seeds in the field, that is, put evil in the hearts of some human beings, so they went away from God and did not give good fruits.
So they asked Him: Shall they gather up the tare plants from among the wheat, that is, pass a sentence of destruction on the wicked in the world?

entries.section: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: God refused to gather up the tares, lest they harm the original wheat plants, in addition to the fact that destroying the wicked deprives them of sufficient opportunity to repent, and may frighten or disturb the children of God, because they see in their God love and tenderness. For if He destroyed all the wicked, they would be terrified and unable to repent and strive because of the intense fear. For Peter who denied repented and became a preacher, and Matthew the tax collector became a disciple, and Paul, who was Saul, the bitter enemy of Christianity, became its servant, and it honored him with the title "the Apostle." Therefore God did not gather up the tares, perhaps by repentance they will turn into wheat.

So the wicked are of two kinds: a kind insisting on its wickedness and this will perish, and the other kind will repent and be saved. So we do not gather up the tares lest we root up the wheat with them, that is, the children of God who have fallen into sin and their appearance became like the tares, but they will repent and return to bear good fruit, that is, become good wheat.
Seize the opportunity of life to repent and cast off the seeds of the tares, so that you may have good fruit and a pure life with God.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: God commanded that all the plants be given a full opportunity to grow, so that the righteous may be tested by their rejecting the evils of the wicked around them, and perhaps the wicked may be enlightened by the light of the righteous and repent and return to God. But if the wicked insist on their wickedness, after death they meet a dreadful fate, which is eternal torment into which they are cast in bundles (groups). Just as they were gathered in evil lusts in the world, they continue together in eternal torment. But the righteous are gathered into the barn of God, that is, His Kingdom, so that each one may enjoy fellowship with God, each according to his toil and his fruits.
(5) The parables of the mustard seed and the leaven (vv. 31-33):

31- Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: 32- Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. 33- Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened."

entries.section: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: The mustard seed: it is the smallest of seeds, but when it is buried in the ground, it is surrounded by darkness and dust, and endures this. And despite its apparent weakness, the Holy Spirit works in it and makes it grow, and it becomes a great tree, larger than the trees of the rest of the herbs, its companions. And because of its size, the birds can find a place in it for their nests.

And the mustard seed signifies the Christian or Christ, who endures sufferings and death, and so has a great life in heaven. And by enduring pain and bearing the Cross, a person's thoughts are raised and become heavenly like the birds soaring in the sky.

And the mustard seed signifies the good news of the Gospel, and the Church which began as a small group within Judea, and within years spread to the whole world, and embraced many souls who believed and began to praise God like the birds.
The mustard seed is like faith, which is tested in afflictions, and so grows and becomes a great tree.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: The woman: she signifies the Church that hides the leaven, that is, Christ, for by His Incarnation He lives in our midst, and so turns the meal, which is mankind, into spiritually active believers, who influence others and draw them to the faith. "Three measures": they point to the spirit, the soul and the body, that is, Christ when He took our human nature raised us to a spiritual nature by His redemption and the work of His Holy Spirit in us.
The woman may also signify the Jews who crucified Christ, and thus by His death and burial He renewed human nature to live with Him.

It is also possible that the woman signifies God who put the leaven, or the Church, in the world, that is, the meal, and it drew souls to the faith, and spread in the whole inhabited world quietly and in love.

Keep the word of God within you, and apply it in your life so that it works in you and changes your thoughts and your conduct, and continue to meditate on it so that the renewal of your life continues. And then you will influence those around you without feeling it, and draw them to life with God.
At this time the teachings of Christ were all in parables. But before this or after it, His teachings were direct, that is, He used all methods of teaching.
"The prophet": that is, the seer, and he is Asaph.

"Kept secret": the spiritual ordering of God for the salvation of man, which it was difficult for man to understand because of his sins, and which Christ declares in the New Testament, and it is His love for mankind which was in His heart from the foundation of the world and the creation of man.

Matthew was accustomed to confirming his words with prophecies, because he addresses the Jews who knew the Holy Scriptures; and God said this in (Ps 78:2): "I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old."

God's love for you is very great from eternity, and He wants to declare it to you if you open your heart and care to hear Him. And you can do that through your seeking Him by reading the Holy Bible, and being bound to the Church, and hearing spiritual sermons, and your care to learn from everyone, especially the Fathers and spiritual brethren.

entries.section: (7) The interpretation of the parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: The treasure: it signifies Christ who is in the Holy Bible.
The field: it signifies the Holy Bible.
"For joy thereof": the spiritual consolations that a person receives through spiritual practices, which move him to give up everything in order to continue enjoying this spiritual feeling.

And in order for us to acquire the Holy Bible in our hearts, and live by it, and enjoy Christ who is in it, we must remove from our hearts our material attachments, and be ready to give up any of them, and by this we imitate Joseph who left his garment in the hand of his master's wife, and accepted to be cast into prison, and was raised to the throne of Egypt and had riches and authority, and even distributed good things to the whole world around him.

And the field also signifies Christ, and the treasure His profound words which the believer submissive to the Holy Spirit understands, who is the one not attached to the world and all its possessions, so that his spirit is free to understand God, and by this God reigns over the heart, and the believer has a portion in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (7) The interpretation of the parable of the tares of the field

paragraphs.text: The one pearl of great price is the love of Christ, and this merchant is the spiritual man who seeks the truth, and tries to acquire pearls, that is, virtues. But the love of Christ surpasses every virtue, and of course surpasses all the possessions of the world, and likewise all material lusts however dazzling they seem. And in his great amazement at the love of Christ, he gives up all that is in the world and considers it refuse, that he may gain Christ. And then He reigns over his heart as a pledge of the eternal Kingdom.

Do not be occupied with the affairs of the world and the needs of the body and the various enticements, rather than the salvation of your soul, but give priority to your relationship with God, and if worldly matters conflict with your spiritual life, be strong and give them up that you may obtain the salvation of your soul, and enjoy serving others to win them by love for Christ.
Christ made sure that His disciples understood His parables, so that they would apply them in their lives.

Christ made clear to His disciples how to be scribes truly learned in the truth, the word of God, and not like the Jewish scribes who were concerned with copying the Holy Scriptures carefully and with precision in the letter, and not with doing them. So He likened the spiritual scribe, who has learned the word of God, to a man who has a house, which is his life depending on the word of God, and he brings out of the Holy Bible useful meanings, whether from the new (the New Testament) or the old (the Old Testament), to live by them, and they guide him in his life with God.
After He had completed His teachings to the crowds and His disciples by these parables, He left the place, and went to another place to continue preaching.

Take care to read the Holy Bible in both its Testaments, to obtain spiritual meanings that you apply in your life every day... By this you take care of the salvation of your soul, and then from what you have experienced you will have something to teach others.

Jesus came to the city of Nazareth where He was brought up, for He was one of its citizens, and entered their Jewish synagogue and taught His powerful teachings, and they marveled greatly at the power of His words and His miracles. It is good for a person to care for the spiritual care of his family and relatives, and even if this is difficult because of their rejection of his words, he can offer this care by praying for them, and indirect teaching such as speaking about what he heard in the sermons of the Church or reading from the Holy Bible and spiritual books. And if he has a standing with them, let him speak directly, and if not, he can recommend some servants of the Church or loved ones connected with spiritual things to draw them to God.

The Jews' wonder did not move them to faith, but they were content only with wonder, since they knew His origin, that He is the son of Mary and Joseph the carpenter, and they also knew the sons and daughters of His mother's sister whose names are mentioned... the sons of Mary, the sister of the Virgin, the wife of Cleophas, and Jewish custom regarded the sons of an aunt and the sons of an uncle as brothers (as is known now in Upper Egypt). So they could not imagine that the awaited Messiah would be an ordinary person coming out from among them, although the prophecies declare this clearly.

Because their minds were confined to His human origin and His relatives, they could not believe in His divinity. And there was a common proverb among them that a prophet is without honor in his own country, so because of their knowing His origin they were accustomed to treat Him as an ordinary man and not a distinguished one.
And because of the weakness of their faith, He did only few miracles among them, because they would not believe Him.

God is ready to work in your life according to your faith and your holding fast to Him and your seeking Him, so open your heart to being discipled and learning at the hands of those around you, and do not belittle any member of your family or your acquaintances, for he may be the divine image that God offers you with simplicity and ease, that you may learn from him, even if he is your little child, or any person of little standing.
The killing of John the Baptist; the feeding of the crowds; the walking on water

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: "At that time": during the preaching of Christ.

"Herod": this is Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great who killed the children of Bethlehem. He is the one to whom Pilate sent the Lord Christ to be tried before His crucifixion. He was ruler over Galilee, Samaria and Perea, which is the northern region of the land of the Jews. When he heard of the preaching of Christ, he thought that He was John the Baptist and that he had risen from the dead after he had killed him, because he feared John and his rebuke of him, since his words were the truth. "Tetrarch": the Romans divided the kingdom of the Jews into four parts, and set Herod Antipas as ruler over one of them.

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Herod desired to marry Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, and he seized her from him while he was still alive, and no one was able to prevent him because of his authority and power. But John the Baptist, the man of the wilderness who fears no one because he relies on God, went in to him in his palace and rebuked him, and called him to leave Herodias and repent. But he did not repent, and he tried to silence John the Baptist and imprisoned him; indeed, he tried to kill him, but he feared the Jews because John was greatly loved and had a large following.

Do not try to silence your conscience and the voice of the Holy Spirit, but submit to it, for it will continue to condemn you if you do not repent, not only on this earth but forever in the final torment. So listen to His voice now and give up your desires, that you may rejoice forever.

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Herod held a great celebration on the occasion of his birthday, which probably included food and much wine, and it was full of revelry and singing.

And the daughter of Herodias by Philip, who was called Salome, arose and danced a lewd dance to entice Herod. She did indeed entice him, to the point that he wanted to reward her at any price, even if he had to give her half of his kingdom. The wine he had drunk may also have helped fill him with lust and lack of balance, so he swore to give her whatever she asked.
Do not yield to lust, lest you lose your balance and your reason and become like the animals, and rush into words you will regret or deeds that defile your life.

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Herodias had persuaded her daughter Salome of the necessity of getting rid of John the Baptist, because he hindered her from remaining queen through her marriage to Herod, and consequently she and her daughter would lose all the grandeur and wealth in which they lived. Indeed, it may have been Herodias who urged Salome to this lewd dance, so as to entice Herod and stir up his lust, so that she could ask him to kill John. Therefore, when Herod asked Salome what she wanted as a reward for her dancing, she answered at once, asking for the head of John on a platter, so that her mother would remain the wife of the king, and would obtain the whole kingdom and not only half of it.

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: When Herod heard that, he awoke from his heedlessness and was greatly grieved, either because he feared John and esteemed him, or because he feared the uproar of the people who loved John. But because of his pride, he could not go back on his oath, although it would have been better if he had humbled himself and refused.
And being a man of lust, he could not refuse the request of the daughter of his beloved, and he commanded that they cut off John's head and bring it on a platter.
Sin puts you in a predicament, but repentance makes you pure, so that you walk in uprightness and peace of mind.

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: They cut off John's head and brought it to the king, who gave it to Salome, and she presented it to her mother Herodias. Thus the wicked Herodias accomplished her purpose, but the voice of truth still rebukes her to this day, and will rebuke her forever while she is in hell.

entries.section: (1) The killing of John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: "His disciples": that is, the disciples of John.

"Told Jesus": because their teacher John had urged them to follow Christ and to take refuge in Him in all their needs; their intention may also have been that Christ should beware of the wicked Herod.
The disciples of John were deeply grieved, and they went and took his body to bury it with honor, and informed Jesus of what had happened.
Thus ended the life of the angel who prepared the way for Christ, after he had proclaimed the voice of truth to all around him.

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: "When Jesus heard": that is, Jesus heard the news of the death of John, and that Herod was saying of Him that He was John risen from the dead.
"By ship": He boarded a ship from Capernaum to the eastern shore of the Sea of Tiberias. "A desert place": a valley near Bethsaida, which lies east of the Sea of Tiberias.
"Apart": His disciples, during that time, had been sent by Him to preach in the villages of Judea (Mk 6:30-31), and they met Him after He came out of the ship.
"The people heard": they learned that He had boarded the ship, heading to the east of the Sea of Tiberias.
"On foot": it seems that the wind was light, so they were able to catch up with Him after He reached the east of the Sea of Tiberias.

Jesus did not resist the evil of Herod, but withdrew to the wilderness, for He had a greater purpose, which was the accomplishment of redemption. He went to a desert place to teach us the importance of solitude and quiet in the lives of the children of God; it is an opportunity for spiritual fullness and self-examination, in order to go forth into service and the doing of good.

When the multitudes learned of it, they followed Him on foot, for He had become beloved by all, because of the greatness of His teachings, the abundance of His miracles, and His tenderness toward all.

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: "When Jesus went forth": He came out of the ship and met His disciples.
"A great multitude": the multitudes who arrived in succession from the cities and villages of Galilee.

"Was moved with compassion": that is, He had pity on them for their ignorance of the way of salvation and their preoccupation with their bodily needs, such as the healing of their diseases, yet they were ready to receive teaching.

Christ received the multitudes with love, healed their sick, and preached to them as was His custom. This was a preparation for them to eat the bread of blessing, just as a person prepares, through repentance and confession, by the healing of his spiritual diseases before partaking of the Holy Mysteries.
His care for the sick took a long time, since the multitudes numbered in the thousands, until evening came (the men among them numbered five thousand).

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: "Evening": the Jews had two evenings, the first in the afternoon, which is the one mentioned here, and the second after it, at sunset, which is the one mentioned in (v. 23).

The disciples took pity on the multitudes and thought that their Teacher was unaware of how late the hour was, so they alerted Him to send them away before darkness fell, especially since they had not eaten since the morning when they gathered around Him, because the place was desolate, outside the cities, with no food in it; and they forgot that Christ was with them, He who satisfies all and who had done many miracles, so how could it be hard for Him to feed them?!

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: The miracle of feeding the multitudes is the only miracle recorded in all four Gospels, because it declares the blessing of Christ that covers all our needs, so that we rely on Him and do not worry about the disturbances of the world. Christ answered His disciples, asking them to give the people food to eat, so that they would take their place as those responsible for this people, and in order to test their faith: would they ask Him, that is, believe in His power, or would they submit to human logic and the lack of food?

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: "We have here": the disciples searched among the multitudes for anyone who had food, and found only this small amount, "five loaves and two fishes", because it seems that the multitudes thought they would return quickly, but the words of Christ and His miracles drew their hearts, so they stayed with Him until the end of the day.

"Five loaves": John (Jn 6:9) mentions that they found with a lad five barley loaves, which is the lowest kind of bread, that is, the food of the poor, but by the blessing of Christ it becomes abundant and satisfies all.

When Christ asked the disciples to feed the people, they did not think of returning to Him to satisfy them, but searched for any food among the people, and found only two fishes and five loaves, so they told Christ of their helplessness and presented to Him the little food they had found.
The five loaves signify the five books of Moses, or the five sacrifices of the Jews, and the five senses of man; they represent man's weak and limited capabilities.
"Two fishes": they signify the teachings of the Old and New Testaments.

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: Christ did not despise these weak capabilities, but asked for them to be brought so that He might bless them. However weak and little your spiritual striving may be, God awaits it attentively to bless it with His grace, and He will satisfy your whole life.

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: "On the grass": the valley in which they were sitting was a place for pasture and not for farming, so it was full of grass.
"Blessed, and brake": the loaf would be large and dry, so He broke it in order to reduce the crumbs of bread left after the meal.

And the blessing was either that the broken piece returned to its first size, so He would break it a second time, and so on... or perhaps that whenever He put His hand into the bag containing the two fishes and the five loaves He found others, or created others, and the distribution continued until all received, or in some other way; what matters is that they increased greatly until the multitudes were satisfied by the abundance of food.
Christ blessed the food after He had made them sit down quietly, and He lifted His eyes to heaven to teach them to pray before eating, asking for the blessing of God.

Then He gave to His disciples to distribute to the people in an orderly way, as Mark the Evangelist mentions (Mk 6:40) that the disciples made the multitudes sit in groups, each group of a hundred or fifty, for they are the priests of the New Testament responsible for shepherding and satisfying the multitudes, and so that no one would be forgotten, for order ensures that the food reaches everyone.

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: The blessing was so great that all the multitudes ate and were filled and there was left over, for God always gives generously.

Then He commanded that the fragments be gathered, out of respect and appreciation for the grace of God, and to show the greatness of the miracle, and the fragments filled twelve baskets, according to the number of the disciples.

And the carrying of the twelve baskets declares that what happened was not a dream or merely a feeling that the multitudes sensed, but a reality. Then, when they departed, they distributed these fragments to the poor whom they found in the villages through which they passed.

entries.section: (2) The feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes

paragraphs.text: The number of the women and children was not mentioned, not out of neglect of them, but because the man is the head of the family and speaks for it. And symbolically, the women signify softness, and the children immaturity. A person should be strong and mature, not pampered.
And the number five thousand points to the five books of Moses, as we mentioned, and the thousand signifies heaven, that is, that the heavenly blessing of God covers all His children.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: "Constrained": either out of compassion for them because of the weariness of the whole day, or because they felt, with the multitudes, that He was the awaited Messiah of whom Moses spoke. For Moses satisfied them with manna from heaven, and here is Christ satisfying them by His blessing from the two fishes and the five loaves. For this reason they tried to make Him king over them, that He might deliver them from the Romans, and the first to sympathize with this thought were the disciples, because of their love for Him; therefore He constrained them to depart. "To go before Him unto the other side": to cross from the east of the Sea of Tiberias to the city of Capernaum. After the miracle of feeding the multitudes, the crowds remained around Him to receive His blessing, to ask Him their various questions, and for Him to complete the healing of their sicknesses.

The disciples tried to help Him in organizing the multitudes, but He sent them away, to go before Him and cross to the other shore of the Sea of Tiberias. And when they tried to wait with Him, He constrained them to go for two spiritual purposes: (1) that He might be alone in the mountain.
(2) that they might face the trials of life and their weakness be revealed, so that He might help them with His power and strengthen their faith.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: "He sent the multitudes away": this took a long time because of their attachment to Him, and in order to complete the healing of their sicknesses.

"The mountain": He went up to it to be away from the multitudes, and it was beside the valley in which they had gathered. One who seeks solitude for prayer tries to keep as far as he can from conversation with people and from many meetings, as some saints did, such as St. Anthony the Great.
"Evening": that is, the hour of sunset.

After Christ blessed the multitudes and sent them away, He went to be alone in the mountain. Thus He repeats the importance of solitude and quiet in our lives, especially before undertaking important works and services.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: The disciples boarded the ship at evening time, and then night came. After a short while, contrary winds rose and hindered the progress of the ship; indeed, the waves beat upon it so that it almost sank, and the disciples, with their experience in sailing the sea, tried to advance the ship, but their attempts did not succeed.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: The disciples remained in great distress until near the end of the night, that is, the fourth watch, which is the end of the period of darkness and about three hours before sunrise, that is, about four o'clock after midnight.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: Before they fell into despair, Christ appeared to them walking on the water, coming toward the ship, and they were afraid of Him, for they supposed Him to be a strange spirit.

And here His divinity and His authority over nature were revealed for the second time, when He broke its laws and walked on the water (the first time was when He "rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm" ch. 8:26).
You too can be above the sea and its waves, that is, the world, if you believe and hold fast to Christ, so that you do not drown in your lusts, but rise above them through repentance.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: Jesus reassured them, saying: It is I, Christ your Teacher. So the fear began to leave them as they heard His voice, which was familiar to them.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: "If it be thou": this does not mean doubt, for Peter could not cast himself into death while doubting the person of Christ; rather it means, since You are Christ, grant me the grace of walking on the water. Peter believed in Christ who walked on the water, and in the impulse of his love he wanted to hasten to Him, so he asked Him to permit him to walk on the water that he might rejoice in meeting Him, and within himself he believed in Christ's authority over that. So Christ commanded him, saying: "Come." And he went down and walked on the water, rejoicing as he advanced toward Christ... Christ did not calm the waves, but gave him authority to walk above them.
Do not wait for Christ to remove the trial, for what matters most is that He gives you peace and faith, so that you are not troubled by it but walk above it.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: Peter walked in faith while he looked at Christ, but when his gaze turned to the waves he felt their violence, and he was afraid and doubted his ability to continue walking on the water, and then he began to sink, and cried out for help to Christ, who stretched out His hand and lifted him, rebuking him for his little faith and doubt.
Fix your gaze on Christ in tribulation, and do not be troubled by its pressures, for He lifts you above it and keeps your peace.

entries.section: (3) The Lord Christ walks on the water

paragraphs.text: After the disciples saw the authority of Christ over nature in His walking on the water, His permitting Peter to do so, and the sudden stilling of the wind when He entered their ship, their faith in Him was strengthened, and they declared this by worshiping Him, glorifying His greatness.

The tradition of the elders is the inherited teaching, handed down from fathers to sons among the Jews, for the interpretation of the Holy Scriptures and everything related to worship. It is a good and necessary thing, for from it the Apostle Paul knew the names of the two magicians who resisted Moses, Jannes and Jambres (2 Tim 3:8), and Jude knew the story of the dispute between the archangel Michael and Satan over the body of Moses the prophet (Jude 9).

So tradition is very important, and the Apostles in the New Testament commanded that it be held fast. But some of the elders of the Jews added strange teachings to the tradition, which God did not mention and which are against His commandments, among them the necessity of washing the hands before eating, and this is what the scribes rebuked the disciples of Christ for, because they did not carry out this tradition. For these scribes and Pharisees came from Jerusalem after the fame of Christ spread, not to learn anything from Him, but to oppose Him and to find fault with Him.

But the tradition of the elders that they mentioned is an additional thing of no value, because the washing of the hands mentioned in the Holy Scriptures was in other circumstances, for purification from certain sins (Lev 12-15).
Christ made clear to them that there are additions to the tradition of the elders that are not sound, and some of them are even against the commandments of God.

The commandment orders the honoring of father and mother (Ex 20:12), and likewise the Law punishes with death the one who despises or curses one of his parents (Ex 21:17). But a strange tradition was added by the elders of the Jews, that a person could offer a gift to the temple, and by this be exempted from honoring his parents, and this is against the spirit of the commandment, for how can the son neglect the needs of his parents on the basis of a sacrifice or offering he has made, and think that this pleases God?!
It is understood from the above that not every tradition among the Jews is sound, and this is what the Scripture calls the tradition of men, whereas sound tradition is very good.

Do not interpret the Holy Bible according to your personal opinion and your purposes, but hold fast to the teachings of the Church and the holy Fathers of the first generations, and submit to the interpretation of the universal Church, and you will understand the true meaning; and be occupied with applying the commandment more than with philosophical inquiries and debate to prove your opinions.

"Ye hypocrites": because you show something other than what is within you, which is that you hold to the law of God with exactness, while the truth is that you please your own purposes, namely offering money to the temple for your benefit, and neglecting the work of mercy even toward parents, and this is clearly against the commandments of God.

Isaiah showed this strange spirit of the scribes and Pharisees (Isa 29:13) (which is clinging to formal worship while the heart is far from God), and any addition to the word of God is the commandments of men, and is not from the commandments of God.
But if it is an oral word that God spoke to Moses and the prophets, or that Christ spoke to His disciples, then this is sound tradition.

"He called the multitude": His conversation with the scribes and Pharisees may have been on one side and not heard by the multitude that followed Him, or it may have been before the multitude, but He directed the speech to the people in order to teach them the spiritual truths, for He is bold, not fearing the opposition of the wicked, and always concerned for the truth.
"Hear, and understand": that is, listen with attention and awareness to what I say.

Christ wanted to bring the multitudes into the depths, so that they would not be content with the superficiality proclaimed by the Pharisees, which is the concern for washing the hands before eating, but would be concerned with what comes out from within a person and appears in his speech, for if it is evil, this defiles him.

And the words of Christ here have no connection with fasting, as the opponents of fasting claim, but are about washing the hands before eating. As for fasting, He affirmed it clearly many times, such as His teaching about fasting in His Sermon on the Mount (ch. 6:16-18).
"Then": after the multitudes and the scribes and Pharisees departed, Christ entered a house with His disciples (Mk 7:17), and this conversation took place.

"Were offended": they were angered and troubled, because He described them as hypocrites, since their teachings are the commandments of men and not the commandments of God, and He means the fifth of the Ten Commandments, concerning the honoring of parents. The disciples warned their Teacher that the Pharisees were troubled by His words, because He had exposed their hypocrisy and their clinging to teachings that are not from God, and which they attach to the tradition of the elders.

Christ made clear to them that submission to the word of God and freedom from hypocrisy are necessary, that we may be branches in the hand of God, who plants them in His Church, for however beautiful the plant may look, if God did not plant it, it will be rooted up and cast into the fire, because it is a tare and not wheat; so also are the hypocritical Pharisees.
He said to them: "Let them alone", meaning that they should disregard them and their teachings, perhaps that when the multitudes leave them they may repent.

And He declared that they are blind to the truth, worshiping their own honor and leading the Jews who follow them with teachings of error, and they are also blind by the misleading teachings of the Pharisees, and if the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit of destruction... that is, He warns His disciples to keep away from the Pharisees and their misleading teachings, so that they would not be influenced by them and go astray from the truth.
Do not be troubled by the distress of the wicked at your words and conduct, but keep away from them so that you are not influenced by associating with them, and pray for them.

"Then answered Peter": Peter replied, and his question to Christ was not on his own behalf, but also on behalf of the rest of the disciples, for he said: "Declare unto us this parable", and afterward Christ addressed them all. "This parable": that is, the words of Christ mentioned in (v. 11), because he felt that it carried other meanings that needed clarification, so he called it a parable.

The disciples, and Peter the most impulsive of them, asked about the meaning of what Christ had said to the multitudes, and Christ marveled at their lack of understanding, after He had explained to them many earlier parables. But, with the gentleness of His fatherhood, He explained to them also His saying that the foods that enter the mouth are turned into nourishment that flows through the body, and the waste is disposed of, so it is material food that does not defile a person, but what harms him of it is disposed of, and these foods have no effect on the soul.
What comes out of a person's mouth, that is, from his heart, expresses him and he is held accountable for it, and not for what he eats.
Then He gave examples of sins, beginning with evil thoughts, as the source of actual sins, such as murder, adultery and theft.
And what is meant by fornication is a kind of adultery, and by blasphemies, abuse against God or people.
Be concerned for the purity of your speech and your conduct, and if you sin, repent, and hold yourself accountable for what is in your heart more than you are concerned with your outward appearance.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: Jesus departed from the region of Gennesaret, perhaps to keep away from the unprofitable discussions of the Pharisees, or from the crowding of the multitudes, and to show His love for the Gentiles, who are many in Tyre and Sidon, since He came for the salvation of the whole world.
"Tyre and Sidon": two cities on the Mediterranean Sea, west of Galilee, in present-day Lebanon.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: "Have mercy on me": because her daughter's illness causes her great pain.

"Son of David": the Jews believed that the Messiah is the son of David, so when they saw the power of Christ and His miracles, they said that He is the son of David, that is, the Messiah. And when this Gentile woman heard of Christ, she called Him as the Jews title Him. When Christ passed by Tyre and Sidon, a Gentile woman came out to Him, of the descendants of Canaan the son of Ham the son of Noah. The Canaanites are the original inhabitants of the Promised Land, before the Jews came with Joshua. Her daughter was insane because a demon was in her (Mk 7:25), and she heard of the healing power of Christ, so she came out asking Him to heal her daughter.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: Christ paid no attention, and went on His way. But she kept crying out, beseeching Him to heal her daughter, so that His disciples' hearts were moved with pity for her, and they asked Him to respond to her cry. And this is what Christ wanted, to move the hearts of the disciples and make them feel their responsibility for the salvation of the whole world, and not only the Jews.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: Christ answered contrary to their request, declaring what the Jews thought and what He began with first, namely that He came for the salvation of the Jews who believe in God. But in truth He came to the Jews first, and then extended afterward to seek all the nations, as proved by His coming to these regions and performing the miracle.

And this method, that is, preaching to the Jews first, was fitting, because they thought that salvation was for them alone, and they would have rejected it if He had declared from the beginning of His preaching that His salvation was for the whole world. But after He convinced them that His salvation is spiritual and not material, from the Romans, He showed that it is a salvation for everyone in the whole world who believes in Him.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: The woman believed that this was the awaited Messiah, the son of David, and that He is the Savior of the world. So she worshiped Him to declare her submission and her faith in Him, and asked Him to help her and heal her daughter.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: Christ pretended not to accept her request, in order to reveal her faith and humility, so He told her that He had come for the salvation of the Jews, who are the children of God by their faith, and that it is not right for the grace of God that belongs to the children to be given and cast to the Gentiles, whom the Jews regard as dogs.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: The woman's wonderful humility appeared, for she said to Him: the crumbs (the very small fragments) that fall from the children's table are enough for me. So she acknowledged that she was of the dogs, but that she needed His grace; and this also showed the extent of her faith and her persistence in prayer.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

paragraphs.text: Finally, the purpose of Christ, His love and His concern for the Gentiles appeared in the person of this woman, for all that went before was to show the extent of her faith, her clinging to Him, her prayers and her humility. So He declared before the multitudes the greatness of her faith, and then granted the healing of her daughter, who returned well at once.

Hold fast to your prayers however long God's answer is delayed, so that you may acquire new virtues, such as humility, and then obtain what you desire; indeed, God will exalt you in His Kingdom before all the heavenly ones.

Christ returned from the borders of Tyre and Sidon beside the Mediterranean Sea to the Sea of Galilee, that is, the Sea of Tiberias, and went up into the mountain, which signifies being raised above earthly matters, so that those who go up to it declare their clinging to Him in their ascent, for they are not mere walkers on the road. He may have gone to the mountain seeking rest, but the multitudes came to Him and He attended to them.
"The God of Israel": it seems that the multitudes were Gentiles, and when Christ healed them they glorified the God of Israel, because they knew that Christ is a Jew.

The multitudes declared their need of Christ, so they brought to Him their beloved ones who were sick with various kinds of diseases, and He healed them all with His tenderness, so that the multitudes marveled at His divine authority in healing all kinds of diseases. And this signifies spiritually the power of Christ, to whom be glory, to heal everyone whose ability to speak, see or move has been hindered by sin, and all glorified God.

God is ready to heal all your diseases and to solve all your problems, especially the spiritual ones. But you must take refuge in Him with much prayer and humility, laying all your needs before Him, confident of His love, which is able to do everything for you.

entries.section: (5) The feeding of the multitudes with the seven loaves

paragraphs.text: Christ continued His care for the multitudes, whether by healing their diseases, or by His spiritual teachings, or by answering their questions.

The time passed without their noticing, so that they spent three days with Him and did not ask for food, being occupied with His words and miracles. Perhaps they had eaten what they had brought from their homes on the first and second days, and on the third day they had no food left, for they did not expect to remain three days away from their homes, but the words of Christ drew them.

What matters is that Christ cared for their material needs, and spoke of it to His disciples to test their faith, especially after they had seen the feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes, but, sadly, they thought with their minds and not with their faith, and declared their inability to provide food for these multitudes in the wilderness, especially since most of the disciples were poor. Care for your spiritual life and rely on God, and be confident that what is difficult for you of your material needs He will provide for you.

entries.section: (5) The feeding of the multitudes with the seven loaves

paragraphs.text: Christ asked His disciples to look for the food that the multitudes had, and they found only seven loaves and a few little fishes.
The number seven signifies the Holy Spirit who works in the Holy Sacraments, which are able to satisfy all the spiritual needs of man.

entries.section: (5) The feeding of the multitudes with the seven loaves

paragraphs.text: Christ commanded His disciples to organize the multitudes, so they made them sit down so that it would be easy to distribute the food to them, and that they might behold quietly the greatness of the miracle. The wonder is that they believed they would eat, although they knew there was no food except the seven loaves and a few little fishes, but this is the faith that rises above reason and affects a person's conduct.

Christ took the bread and the fishes, and gave thanks, as in the previous miracle, to teach us to pray before taking food, and He blessed with His divine hand, and broke the bread and gave to His disciples to distribute from it, and likewise from the fish, to all the multitudes sitting on the ground; for the disciples are the priests of the New Testament responsible for distributing the gifts of God to all the faithful.

entries.section: (5) The feeding of the multitudes with the seven loaves

paragraphs.text: All ate, and their number was about four thousand men, besides women and children. And the number four signifies the four corners of the world, north and south, east and west, and the number thousand signifies heaven, that is, that the blessing of Christ is for the whole world, satisfying it and raising it to the heavenly life. After all had eaten, the disciples gathered the remaining fragments, and they filled seven baskets, and this also points to the work of the Holy Spirit, for He satisfies all and overflows.
And after Christ blessed the multitudes and sent them away, He boarded the ship on the Sea of Galilee and went to a city called Magdala.
The persecution of the Pharisees, bearing the cross

entries.section: (1) The Pharisees ask for a sign

paragraphs.text: The Pharisees differ from the Sadducees, but their fear of Christ, to whom the multitudes were drawn and left them, made them agree to tempt Him, trying to show His weakness and to turn the multitudes away from Him. So they asked Him to perform for them a great miracle, appearing clearly in the sky or coming down from heaven, to confirm that He is the awaited Messiah, although He had performed many miracles before the multitudes. But in their pride and jealousy they did not believe in Him, and they still opposed Him. And they thought that by asking Him for a great sign from heaven they would reveal His inability to accomplish it, and the multitudes would turn away from Him.

entries.section: (1) The Pharisees ask for a sign

paragraphs.text: "Evening": the hour of sunset.

"The sky is red": at sunset, when the disk of the sun begins to disappear, it gives a red color in the sky, and the clearer it is, the clearer the weather, because there are no clouds covering the red color.
"Red and lowering": the red color at sunrise, if it is not clear because clouds appear, means that the day is wintry and it may rain.
"The face of the sky": that is, the appearances of the weather from which you infer the weather conditions.

"The signs of the times": these are the prophecies that speak of Christ, then the appearance of John the Baptist who preceded Him, and also His many miracles that had not appeared before with such power in Israel, all of which confirm that He is the awaited Messiah. Christ did not give them a miracle, because He did not come to display His power before people, but to save them from sin. And He answered those who tempted Him that God had given them the mind with which they can discern the state of the weather, by the presence of a shining sun or of clouds. If they were able to discern the state of the weather, why did they not rather care to know the prophecies written about Him?! For this is their basic work as the religious leaders of the Jewish community, that they believe in Him and lead everyone to faith.

entries.section: (1) The Pharisees ask for a sign

paragraphs.text: Christ made clear the reason for their lack of understanding, which is the evil of their hearts and their jealousy of Him. They clung to their selfishness and left God, so they became, spiritually, adulterers and fornicators, that is, they worshiped their pride instead of God. Therefore, He called them to repentance, saying to them that they did not need to see a sign from heaven, but should remember the story of Jonah the prophet and the people of Nineveh, and repent as they did, and then it would be easy for them to believe in Him. And He left them, grieved for them, so as not to waste His time in discussions without benefit.

Do not be much occupied with material requests from God, and know that your first need is repentance, that you may become pure, and be confident that if you care only for repentance, God will provide all your material needs.

The disciples crossed by ship from Magdala, on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, to the eastern shore. And in their absorption in service, they forgot their material needs, that is, taking food for the journey. The servant or the spiritual person forgets some of his material needs while occupied with God, but God provides for him.

Christ warned His disciples privately, away from the multitudes, of the leaven of the Pharisees, and by this He means their hypocrisy, for they teach exacting religious teachings, but in order to display their honor before people, and not out of love for God.

And leaven resembles hypocrisy, because it spreads inwardly in the dough without anyone sensing it, like the cunning of the hypocrite who pretends to be pious while his heart is far from the love of God.
But the disciples thought He was speaking of the leaven of material bread, that is, He was reminding them that they had forgotten to take food for the journey.

The words of Christ exposed a sin in the hearts of the disciples, namely their preoccupation with material needs, for they were troubled because they had forgotten the food needed for the journey. So Christ rebuked them, reminding them of His miracles of feeding the multitudes with the five loaves or the seven loaves, and how they were filled and twelve baskets or seven baskets were left over. They should have relied on Him, confident of His ability to provide for their material needs, and focused only on the service.

Then the disciples understood the purpose of Christ, that He was warning them of the teachings of the Pharisees, full of hypocrisy, that is, He was calling them to simplicity of heart and the love of God and of everyone.

Do not rejoice in your ability to pretend to what is not within you in order to reach your purposes, for this makes you divided against yourself, and people with time do not trust you; but apply in your life what you believe, and if there is evil within you, repent of it and be rid of hypocrisy.
Christ wanted to direct His disciples to knowing Him and believing in His divinity, so He asked them what is the people's belief concerning Him?

The disciples replied that there are many opinions, for some, like Herod, think that He is John the Baptist risen from the dead, and some say that He is Elijah who ascended to heaven in his body and has returned to earth, for the Jews were awaiting the coming of Elijah before the coming of the Messiah, based on the prophecy of Malachi (Mal 4:5-6), (and others think He is Jeremiah the prophet, and some said that He is one of the ancient prophets who has risen, because of the similarity of His message with the message of the prophets who called people to repentance in preparation for eternity, but they could not understand anything about His divinity.

Then Christ moved to the important question, which is the faith of His disciples concerning Him, and Peter answered on behalf of the disciples, declaring that they believe in Him as the awaited Messiah, the Son of God, that is, God incarnate.
"Flesh and blood": that is, a human being.
"My Father which is in heaven": by the Spirit of God, for it is a revelation from heaven by the power of God, because faith in the incarnate Christ rises above reason and human logic.

Christ praised the faith of Peter which he declared, and it is clear that this was by the grace of God and not from human logic, because the mystery of the Incarnation surpasses reason; for how does God condescend, in His love and humility, to unite with our humanity?!

Christ affirmed the importance of this declared faith, for upon the rock of faith the Church is built, so the basis of anyone's membership in the Church is his faith that Christ is God. And He declared that Satan and hell have no authority over the Church, for her children, the faithful, after this life are transferred to the paradise of bliss and the Kingdom of Heaven.
And He did not say to him, You are the rock, but said: "Thou art Peter", to make clear that the rock is the rock of faith upon which the Church is built, and not Peter.

"Keys": He likened the Church to a locked treasure, and gave the keys to the Apostles and their successors, the bishops and priests, to give from God absolution through forgiveness to the one who repents, or binding and withholding from the Holy Sacraments from the one who refuses repentance.
"The kingdom of heaven": that is, the Church, where God reigns over the hearts of His faithful children, and this Church extends forever.

Since Christ had spoken of the Church in which the Holy Spirit works, He declared the sacrament of confession, in which authority is given to the Apostles, which is the authority of loosing and binding. So everyone who persists in his sins, they bind his sins upon him, and he is not worthy to partake of the Holy Sacraments, and everyone who repents and confesses them, they loose him from them and give him the Sacraments.

Christ gave this authority to Peter as the representative of the priesthood of the New Testament, that is, to all the disciples and their successors, the bishops and priests, and He will repeat the same authority once more in (ch. 18:18).

And this is the first clear declaration of the institution of the sacrament of repentance and confession, one of the seven sacraments of the Church, and He declared it early because of its importance, since repentance is the entrance to the whole spiritual life.

After His clear declaration of His divinity, He charged His disciples not to speak of this matter to the multitudes, lest they stir up the envy of the Pharisees and the religious leaders, and hinder the people's faith in Him. And after the accomplishment of redemption on the cross and the announcement of His resurrection, this teaching will strengthen their faith.

Your faith in Christ makes you not troubled by the changes of the world, but rejoicing in fellowship with Him, and preparing for being with Him always in His heavenly Kingdom, and it also drives you to serve Him in drawing distant souls so that they enter His Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

paragraphs.text: "The elders": the leaders of the Jews, members of their highest council, which is the Sanhedrin (ch. 5:21-22).
"The chief priests": the current high priest, the former chiefs, and the heads of the divisions of the priests.
"The scribes": the copyists and teachers of the Law.

After Christ declared His divinity to His disciples, and the founding of His Church which stands forever, it was necessary to declare the price of establishing this Church, that is, the shedding of His blood on the cross. So He made clear to His disciples the necessity of the sufferings He would receive from the elders and chief priests, which would lead in the end to His death to redeem mankind; but He would rise afterward on the third day. For after they knew His divinity, they could understand His resurrection, and not be troubled by His sufferings.

entries.section: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

paragraphs.text: "Took him": Peter thought that the words of Christ about His sufferings were a kind of emotion resulting from the great opposition of the Jews to Him, so he tried to prevent Christ from speaking these words, lest it affect the rest of the disciples with grief and despair.
"Rebuke": he tries to prevent Him from continuing these talks.
"Be it far from thee": Peter believed in His divinity, and he and the rest of the disciples did not understand the idea of redemption, and he saw that sufferings contradict His power.
"Satan": because his thinking is satanic, as he thinks of the earthly kingdom and not the heavenly kingship. "An offence": you are trying, Peter, to hinder the redemption of mankind.
"Those that be of men": that is, the earthly kingship, and not the thought of God, which is the redemption of mankind.

The disciples were affected by what Christ would suffer, because He demolished the idea of the earthly kingdom, which they believed in with the rest of the Jews, and Peter rushed to prevent Christ from handing Himself over to the priests by going to Jerusalem. But Christ rebuked Peter because he was hindering the redemption of mankind, by his clinging to the earthly kingship and his position in this kingdom, forgetting the most important thing, which is the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

paragraphs.text: Christ declared the two conditions of following Him in order for a person to become a member of this Church, which are: (1) denying oneself, that is, humility.
(2) bearing the cross, that is, enduring sufferings for the sake of holding to the faith and the commandments of God.

And since the way seemed hard, Christ made clear that saving the soul from the sins of the world requires losing it, in the sense of rejecting and putting to death every evil desire in the soul, and whoever loses his soul, that is, bears the cross for the sake of Christ, rescues it from being lost in the evils of the world, and finds a place for it in the Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

paragraphs.text: On the other hand, if a person permits himself the lusts of the world, and even if we imagine that he possessed every desire in him, he will lose his eternity, and by this he will have lost everything, because there is nothing equal to this soul or compensating for it. For a person has one soul and cannot find another, and it is more precious than all the possessions of the world and its lusts, and its price is the blood of Christ shed for it, so a person cannot lose the most precious thing in existence, which is himself, for the sake of any temporary material desires.

entries.section: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

paragraphs.text: "The Son of man": Christ is not ashamed to call His name in heaven the Son of Man, for as He shared with us weakness in the body on earth, He makes us share with Him in the heavenly glory, and remains among us as the firstborn among many brethren.
Here Christ warns them of the Day of Judgment, when He comes in the glory of His Father with His angels, and judges every person according to his faith, his love for Him, and all his works.

By this He reassures His followers that what they endure on earth, they will receive its reward on the Day of Judgment. And on the contrary, the wicked who delighted in sin will be punished on that day.

entries.section: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

paragraphs.text: The coming of the Son of Man in His kingdom may be meant to refer to His transfiguration on the mountain before His three disciples: Peter, James and John.

It may also be that what is meant is the spread of faith in Christ and His reign over hearts in the different countries of the world, and this was witnessed by many of the disciples who lived a long time, such as John the Beloved who lived until near the end of the first century.

Do not be dazzled by the passing lusts of the world, or occupied with its cares and the needs of the body. And do not let your standards be material like the rest of people, but seek the salvation of your soul through the growth of your relationship with God and the service of others, preferring the work of mercy to your own comfort, and accept with joy all the sufferings that God permits for you, training yourself each day to control your desires and to use everything in measure, so that your feelings may be released in love toward God, and you prepare yourself for eternity.
The Transfiguration, paying the taxes

Six days after informing them of the news of His sufferings and death, Christ went up with three of His close disciples, whom He had chosen to accompany Him at the raising of the daughter of Jairus, and to enter with Him into the depths of the Garden of Gethsemane before His arrest, because of their spiritual readiness to understand lofty matters more than the rest. For He wants to reveal everything to everyone, but not everyone wants to understand, and these had greater love for Him.

"Six": this number signifies the completion of human work, but it is less than the number seven, which is the completion of the divine work by the Holy Spirit. When a person completes what he is able to do of striving, the grace of God reveals to him the divine help. The Transfiguration was to support the disciples, so that they would not be wearied and doubt when they saw His crucifixion and death. And He took the three because "in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established", and they represent all mankind, like the three sons of Noah.
He took them up on a high mountain, since it is necessary, with toil, to rise above limited earthly thinking in order to ascend to heavenly things, so that God may reveal Himself to us.

Christ revealed some of the brightness of His divinity, as much as His three disciples could bear, for the greatest light they know is the sun, and so His face became, for He is the Sun of Righteousness who lights our lives. As for His garments, they became white as the light, and garments are what cling to the body, so they signify the Church that is enlightened by Christ.

Moses appeared, who represents the Law, and Elijah, who represents the prophets, because in Christ the Law and the prophecies of the prophets are fulfilled, and to confirm that He fulfills the Law and establishes all the teachings of the prophets. Moses died and then appeared in a spiritual body, whereas Elijah ascended in his body and came to appear in this Transfiguration. For Christ is the God of the living and the dead, because the spirits of those who died are kept with Him.

Moses and Elijah spoke of the redemption which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem (Lk 9:31), for it is the goal of the Law and the prophets, that is, the salvation of the world, and the disciples probably knew the persons of Moses and Elijah from Christ's calling them and speaking with them. The following appears from the Transfiguration:
(1) That those who have fallen asleep, like Moses, are still alive with God.
(2) That the spirits in heaven know one another.
(3) That the saints in heaven care about our salvation.
The disciples rejoiced greatly at this divine sight, and enjoyed seeing Moses and Elijah, and wished that this sight would not end.

And from his joy and admiration at the greatness of this Transfiguration, Peter rushed forward as was his habit, and expressed the feelings of the disciples by proposing to Christ the making of three tabernacles, so that they might remain a longer time in this place; and he did not understand that these spiritual beings do not need tabernacles to shelter them.

While Peter was dazzled and attached to the sight of the Transfiguration, Christ saw that they could not bear to see His divinity more than this, so a bright cloud came, signifying the luminous indwelling of God, and Christ, Moses, Elijah and the three disciples disappeared inside it. And in this fearful sight inside the cloud, they heard a voice from heaven declaring that Christ is the beloved Son, to whom all people must submit and listen; for the Father testifies that Christ is the Son of God, the Only-Begotten Son.

The disciples were greatly afraid when they entered the cloud and no longer saw anything, neither Christ nor Moses and Elijah, nor each one his two companions. And before the awe of the Father's voice from heaven, they fell on the ground in their weakness as human beings, but Christ the Redeemer is able to raise them from earthly things to heavenly things.

Christ touched His disciples, and so supported and encouraged them, and they rose to find that the sight of the Transfiguration had ended, and Jesus, whose appearance they were accustomed to, standing alone with them in His ordinary human form.
By this, the Holy Bible confirms that one thing is needful, which is looking to Christ our God and Savior.

Christ charged them not to tell the rest of the disciples or the multitudes of the sight of the Transfiguration until after His resurrection from the dead, because the hearers would not believe, and it would stir up the scribes and Pharisees against them, as they would appear before them as liars, claiming things that in their view were not true. And if some believed their words, this might lead them to confirm the idea of the earthly kingship they long for, so that they would move away from the spiritual, heavenly kingship that Christ intends.
But after the resurrection, the sight of the Transfiguration would support His divinity, and they would be assured of it even more after the Holy Spirit came upon them, that is, with the help of God.

Christ is ready to be transfigured before you if you desire it, indeed He is being transfigured in fact, but you may not notice it because of your many material preoccupations. He speaks to you through the Holy Bible and the guidance of the Church, and even through the events of life and the remarks of those around you, and in various ways calls you to repentance and to knowing Him and living with Him. And the more attentively you listen, the more His appearing to you increases in simple, clear ways, and you enjoy fellowship with Him always.

As the three disciples were coming down from the mountain with Christ, and this was at dawn, since the Transfiguration probably happened at night, because Luke the Evangelist also mentions that when they came down from the mountain on the next day, that is, after the night had passed (Lk 9:28-37), they asked Christ about what the scribes say, that Elijah must first come again to the earth: was this fulfilled by the Transfiguration of Christ on the mountain, or is it another coming, since Elijah did not die but ascended alive to heaven?
And the second coming of Elijah was mentioned in the prophecy of Malachi (Mal 4:5).

Christ affirmed that Elijah will come again to call people to repentance, and this will happen immediately before the Day of Judgment, in the midst of the surge of evil, to bring people back to faith, in the last opportunity available to mankind before the judgment.

Christ pointed here to the spiritual coming of Elijah, where John the Baptist came with the same character as Elijah, that is, detachment from material things and strength in proclaiming the truth. The Baptist suffered from the opposition of the scribes and Pharisees to him, just as they do to Christ the Son of Man, and the Jews did not know that John had come in the spirit of Elijah, that is, with his same character.

"They have done unto him whatsoever they listed": that is, they opposed him and were pleased at his killing, for although the killer was Herod, had it not been for the opposition of the chief priests to him, he would not have been able to kill him because he feared the people.

"The disciples understood": the disciples did not understand until He explained to them the details of John's preparing the way for Him, and they knew that the talk was about John who came in the spirit of Elijah.

God alerts us to repentance in many ways however evil we are, so may we respond quickly to His calls, for He is a tender Father who will support us and give us strength to reject the enticements of sin.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of the demon that the disciples could not cast out

paragraphs.text: After the divinity of Christ appeared in the Transfiguration, the weakness of Satan appears before Him, as a man came to Him and worshiped Him, asking Him to heal his son who had a demon that throws him on the ground unconscious, and sometimes throws him into the fire or the water to kill him, and they rescue him with difficulty. This represents the wicked person subject to the devil, who loses his peace and balance, and the devil tries to destroy him by throwing him into various lusts.
And the man added that the disciples of Christ were unable to cast it out, although they had cast out other demons when He sent them to preach in Judea.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of the demon that the disciples could not cast out

paragraphs.text: Christ rebuked the weakness of faith of His disciples, and the man whose son had a demon, who represents the whole multitude, and He rebuked also their perverseness, that is, their doubt of the power of God and their preoccupation with worldly lusts, because the scribes seized the opportunity of the disciples' inability to cast out the demon, and began to argue with them, showing their helplessness and casting doubt on the standing of their Teacher Jesus.

And He rebuked their weakness, because He had left them for a little while, and the weakness of their faith appeared. And this was beneficial for the disciples and for the multitude, so that they would know that the source of their power is Christ, and would always take refuge in Him, and be able to do everything. Then He rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, who was restored to health.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of the demon that the disciples could not cast out

paragraphs.text: "A grain of mustard seed": the smallest of seeds in size, and it signifies very small faith.

After the multitudes departed, the disciples asked Christ why they were unable to cast out this demon, and He assured them that the reason was their unbelief, and He showed that the power of faith, however small, can move a mountain; and this actually happened in the moving of the Mokattam mountain in Cairo in the year 970 AD in the time of Anba Abraam ibn Zaraa the Syrian (Pope 62).
And what is meant is not only the ordinary mountain, but even more sins and evil lusts, which are harder than ordinary mountains.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of the demon that the disciples could not cast out

paragraphs.text: Christ declared that to overcome Satan, we need faith that appears in deep prayers, and fasting, because it is detachment from the worldly desires that the devil uses to entice us. Consequently, we rob him of his power and overcome him by the power of God; in addition, fasting shows our love for God more than for food and material things. If God permits your weakness to appear at times, it is so that you may examine yourself and take refuge in Him, and so receive greater strength and advance in your spiritual life, so do not be troubled by weaknesses and falls, but rise quickly, confident that you are the beloved child of God, able by His power to overcome all the power of Satan.

entries.section: (5) The tribute of the two drachmas

paragraphs.text: The priests of the Jews used to take two drachmas every year from every Jewish person for the needs of the temple, and the drachma at that time was a coin of small value. The tax collectors came to Capernaum and asked Peter about Christ's paying this tax, so that if He did not pay it, regarding Himself as a prophet, they would find a charge against Him that He was against the temple and did not care for its needs, and if He paid the two drachmas, He was an ordinary person and not the awaited Messiah, because the Messiah in their view would possess an earthly kingdom.
And this tax is not compulsory from the state, but a sign of the Jew's concern for the service and worship of the temple.

entries.section: (5) The tribute of the two drachmas

paragraphs.text: "Yes": that is, yes, and so agreement to pay the tax.

Christ knew of the conversation that took place between the tax collectors and Peter without hearing it, because He is God who knows everything. So He took the initiative of asking Peter about the collecting of taxes, whether it is from the children (the Jews) or from strangers? Peter said to Him: From strangers. Then Jesus said to him: Then are the children free from paying taxes, that is, Christ is the Son of God and the Lord of the temple, so naturally He does not pay the tax.

"Their children": He means the awaited Messiah and the prophets, and no tax is taken from these because they are the owners of the temple. "Strangers": He means the rest of the Jews other than the prophets.
Submit to the order that exists in society, even if it is not sound in your view, out of respect for its laws, since your heart is occupied with what is more important, that is, eternity.

entries.section: (5) The tribute of the two drachmas

paragraphs.text: Because the priests of the Jews did not yet believe, He said to Peter: lest we offend them, I will pay the tax. And Christ directed him to the work he knew, which is catching fish, so he would cast a hook into the sea, and the fish he caught first, he would open its mouth and find in it a stater, which is a coin equal to four drachmas, and he would pay the tax for Christ and for himself.

And by this the authority of Christ over animals appears, and His knowledge of the unseen, that is, of the presence of a stater in the mouth of the fish, and then He directs it to come up on the hook.
His love and care for His disciple Peter also appear, as He pays the tax for him.

And the poverty of Christ and most of His disciples also appears, as He had no money at all, not even a little. Be confident that your God, the Almighty, is able to do everything and meets your needs, so do not be troubled by those who oppose you.
Stumbling blocks, forgiveness

The disciples were still thinking of the Kingdom of Heaven in a human way, so they asked to know who is the greatest in heaven. This shows discussions and thoughts within them about who is the greatest among them, and who will be chief in the new kingdom; and the love of chief place is of course a kind of pride.

Christ's reply to them was that the greatest is the humble, innocent one who loves everyone. And He gave them His answer in a practical way, for He set a child in the midst of them, and asked them to become like him in humility, innocence and love, for these are the conditions for entering the Kingdom. It is to be noted that He did not answer their question, which was who is the greatest, but declared the conditions for entering the Kingdom, so that it might be understood that with the love of chief place and pride they will not enter the Kingdom.

Christ finally answered their question, that the greatest is the humble and innocent one who obeys the commandments of God like this child, and according to the degree of distinction in becoming like children, a person enjoys Christ in eternity.
"In my name": that is, for the sake of Christ.

On another side, Christ honored childhood, which was neglected at that time by all classes of the world, whether Romans, Greeks or Jews, for He declared that childhood belongs to Him, so whoever receives a child and cares for him and is concerned for him is like one who received Christ Himself, because this receiving means love and tenderness. People are concerned with hosting and receiving the rich, but Christ directs their eyes to receiving the weak, the despised and the needy, because concern for them is concern for Christ.
Be concerned, not only for children, but for every person who has no one to look after him or who suffers weakness, for your love offered to him pleases God as if it were offered to Him personally.
"Little ones": any person weak in his abilities who can be made to fall into sin, and this includes in truth all the faithful, because all are liable to fall into sin.
"The depth of the sea": the fullness of the sea and its depth.

A stumbling block is a doubled sin, for a person falls into sin and makes another fall.
