But the chief or master or spiritual teacher takes his authority from Christ, and teaches the teachings of Christ and not his own personal teachings, as is proved by the fact that the Holy Bible in the New Testament calls us to honor those in authority and submit to them (Rom 13:1-2). Likewise St. Paul says of himself that he is a father: "For though ye have ten thousand instructers in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel" (1 Cor 4:15).

And he also calls Onesimus his son, saying: "I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds" (Phlm 10). And St. John the Beloved calls his people his children (1 Jn 2:1; 3:18; 3 Jn 4). As for the title "my lord", Paul and Silas did not object when the jailer of Philippi said to them: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" (Acts 16:30).

Here Christ asks the disciples and their successors the bishops, who preside over the Church and are called fathers of it, not to call anyone father to themselves, because God is their Father, that is, they are responsible for leading the Church. But the meaning is not literal but spiritual, for some fathers can call their fathers spiritually, such as the father of confession; indeed in humility they learn from all the fathers, the bishops and priests, and their fathers in the flesh. And the New Testament esteems the existence of teachers, saying: "or he that teacheth, on teaching" (Rom 12:7).

In sum, they should not act alone in authority and teachings from themselves, but by the authority of God and His word, and should not be led after any of the fathers if he teaches teachings outside the Church and Christ, like the heretics.
Then He calls them clearly to humility before one another, and whoever humbles himself, God glorifies and exalts him, but whoever is proud falls from God's sight, and He rejects him.
"Hypocrites": you pretend to lead the people to the worship of God, though in truth you keep them away from faith in Christ and from walking in the spirit of the commandment.

The Pharisees shut up the kingdom of heaven against themselves by their pride and superficiality and their distance from carrying out the commandments, and they shut it also in the face of the people by making the commandments difficult in their sight, for they loaded them with burdens hard to bear, and also made them stumble by their wrong conduct, so that they kept people away from eternal life.

"For a pretence": that is, for a personal reason and purpose, for by prolonging their prayers, people trust them and give them the guardianship of the widows' money, but sadly they are not faithful with it, but out of their greed they steal from it for their personal benefit.

The hypocrisy of the Pharisees extended, for they were not content with hindering others from entering the Kingdom, but held fast to the appearance of prayer and its prolonging to gain the praise of people, and not from love of God. And their hearts were filled with love of money, so that they exploited the weak such as widows and wronged them and took their money, and did not feel that this was exploitation and wrong, because they were absorbed in love of money and pride.
"Sea and land": that is, great effort to draw a person to the Jewish faith.
"Proselyte": a pagan who enters the Jewish faith.
"The child of hell": deserving eternal torment.

"Twofold": that is, his torment is greater in eternity, because, after he knew faith in God and was made to stumble by the Pharisees, he considers permissible his old sins in which he used to live during his paganism.

The Pharisees strive to bring one of the honorable, wealthy pagans into the faith, and they make great effort because God's help does not assist them, and then after his belief, he discovers their hypocrisy and the distance of their hearts from God, so he stumbles in them and in the Jewish religion, and departs from God, and so deserves eternal torment more than before, since after he knew the faith he denied it.

Beware of being a stumbling block to others by your sins, so that you give a bad picture of God and His Church. And do not be self-seeking in any worship, but offer it out of love of God, and you will gain the salvation of your soul, and spontaneously win those around you for Christ.

Because the Pharisees were occupied with love of money, they taught that whoever swears by the gold that he offers to the Temple is bound to carry out what he swore by. But whoever swears by the Temple may go back on what he swore by. How can this be, when the Temple is of course greater than the gold that is offered to it?! But because of their concern with collecting money, they taught this corrupt teaching.
"The altar": this is the bronze altar at the entrance of the Temple, on which the sacrifices and offerings of the people were offered.

The Pharisees also teach that whoever swears by the offering must fulfil what he swore by. But whoever swears by the altar, it is not important that he fulfil what he promised, so that they may obtain the offerings presented by the people as a material gain for themselves, unconcerned with worship, and with encouraging people in promises to God and life with Him.

In sum, whoever swears by something swears by it and by everything it contains, and this is a logical matter. And the oath was permitted in the Law of Moses, on condition that it be truthful and that its maker keep to it, but they broke the commandment of the oath by their holding fast to their material gains.

And Christ directed their attention to the spirit of the oath, which is swearing by God, the Lord of the altar and the Temple and heaven. How then do they neglect God out of preoccupation with their material benefit, and give interpretations that God did not speak? For God's purpose in the commandment of the oath in the Old Testament was to establish His people's faith in Him and their keeping away from swearing by pagan gods. Do not interpret the word of God according to your personal purposes, but submit to it and do not deceive yourself, and you will receive God's blessings in your life.

The scribes and Pharisees took care to offer tithes of unimportant plants, which might be grown in small quantities in house gardens, such as mint, anise and cummin, to appear exacting in everything. And because the leaders of the Jews benefit from the collection of these tithes, they neglected at the same time the essence of the relationship with God, which is truth, mercy and faith.

And Christ does not reject the offering of tithes, even in small matters. But let us understand the spirit of the commandment and not its literalness, so that we offer tithes in faith in God's blessing and as mercy to the needy and in clinging to God who is the Truth, and walk in mercy, truth and faith in all our life, and not like the scribes and Pharisees, whose hardness of heart appeared in wronging widows and the weak, and who refused to believe in Christ.
"These": refers to offering tithes in everything.
"Those": that is, holding fast to mercy, truth and faith.

Christ describes them as blind because they refused to see the truth that is in Him, and held fast to exactness in small matters, which He likens to the gnat, and neglected the essence of the commandments, which He likens to the camel. They used to strain water and wine lest a gnat be in it, which is considered unclean according to the commands of the Law. But with this exactness they overlook great sins, such as arresting Christ and crucifying Him though He was innocent.

Here the hypocrisy of the Pharisees appears more clearly than in the previous sins, since they care about the exacting appearance of worship, while their hearts are full of evil. And Christ draws their attention to the importance of what is inside the cup and the platter (the dish), and not only cleansing them on the outside, by keeping away from all personal uncleanness, because their food and drink, which they gathered by greed and evil, are not helped by cleansing the vessels outwardly, but by purifying their hearts. And He calls the Pharisee blind, because he does not see the truth of the matter, and is occupied only with appearances.

The Law required not touching the dead or his grave, lest a person be defiled (Num 19:16, 18), so the Jews took care to whitewash their graves, so that passersby would notice them and not touch them. Christ likens the hypocritical life of the Pharisees to the graves that they take care to paint white, so that they appear beautiful outwardly. But inside there are bones and a foul smell like the evil that is in their hearts. Their appearance is exactness and holding fast to worship, but their hearts are hard and their conduct evil.
Care for your repentance and your love for God and for others, and your works and worship will be an expression of your good heart.

Christ also rebukes the Pharisees for resisting the truth while pretending to righteousness, for they build and adorn the tombs of the prophets, and declare their rejection of the evils of their fathers who tortured and killed those prophets, though their works are as evil as their fathers', and they resisted the righteous who are greater than the prophets in their generation, namely John the Baptist and then Christ Himself.

So this speech of yours declares that you are the sons of the killers of the prophets, and not only this, but your present evils in resisting me and my disciples confirm your hypocrisy and the outward show of your righteousness, while your hearts are full of evil. And the truth is that by what you do, you fill up the cup of evil that your fathers made until it overflows, and you are condemned to eternal torment in the end.
Encourage good and help in it with all your heart and all your energy, and you will become a child of God, for everything that leads to good, God rejoices in it.
"Serpents": He likened them to them because of their cunning and their insistence on doing evil.

"Generation of vipers": because their fathers were wicked, for they tortured and killed the prophets in the past. All the preceding sins necessarily deserve the fire of hell, and all the show of worship and false righteousness does not exempt them from it.

Despite the evil of the Jews, God continues to do good to them, so He sends His messengers, whom He called by the names known for teachers among the Jews, namely prophets and wise men and scribes, to declare His voice to the people so that they would repent. But the Jews rise against them and scourge them and torture them and drive them out, and even kill them, because they are insistent on evil.
The synagogues: these are the places of reading and preaching for the Jews in all their cities, and in them they judge those whom they regard as guilty of evil and of violating the Law.

In the end, God will judge them for their resisting the truth and refusing to hear His voice, by killing His innocent men, from the first martyr in the world, who is righteous Abel, to Zacharias son of Barachias, who is the father of John the Baptist, who was killed after he placed the child John on the altar when the soldiers pursued him, saying to them: I took him from the altar and to it I return him. Then the angel of God came and snatched him from the altar, but him they killed.
And thus He depicts the Jewish nation as one person, whom God punishes for all the blood of the martyrs in the Old Testament before Christianity.

Know that God is a just Judge, so do not go on in your selfishness or your wronging of others, whatever your authority or your logical argument, but repent in humility and correct your errors, and you will receive His mercies.
This divine punishment was accomplished in that generation of the Jews by the destruction of Jerusalem and the killing of those in it in AD 70 at the hand of Titus, the commander of the Romans.

Christ likens Himself to the hen that gathers her eggs under her until they hatch and the chicks come forth to life, but the feathers of the mother hen fall off, that is, she gives her life to bring her children forth to life, as Christ suffered and died for us; and He offered His love to the sons of the killers of the prophets, but they rejected His teachings that were for their salvation, and even rose against Him and crucified Him.

The Temple was spiritually desolate because of the evil of the priests, scribes and Pharisees, and Christ left it after that, that is, He took His blessing away from it, and then its destruction was accomplished at the hand of the Romans in AD 70.

A few days after this talk, Christ was crucified and died, and the Jews did not see Him, because after His resurrection He appeared to a small number, namely His disciples and some believers. But the Jews who will believe and become Christians will rejoice on the Day of Judgment at the Second Coming of Christ, and say: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord" (Ps 118:26), just as the disciples and believers rejoiced in Christ when He appeared to them after His resurrection, saying the words of the aforementioned psalm; and thus everyone who believes in Christ shares with the Apostles, and feels that the blessed Christ has come and dwelt in him by faith.
Signs of the destruction of Jerusalem; the Second Coming

Christ sat with His disciples on the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, and from there the Temple is clearly visible. The disciples asked Christ about the time of the destruction of the Temple, and they also asked Him about His second coming, and what the signs are that appear before His coming, so that they might take heed and be prepared.

From this it appears that Christ's answer includes two subjects, namely the destruction of Jerusalem and His second coming. We shall notice their overlapping, because the lesson drawn from them is one, namely repentance and preparation. The Jews used to think that their Temple would remain until the end of days, and the disciples thought that its destruction would be at the end.

Christ warned them of the appearance of false pretenders, each of whom says that he is the Christ, or who come as though they were messengers from Him; so they must be examined, and one must not be led after them. And if they do not say words that agree with the word of the Holy Bible and the Church, they are liars, so we reject them.

Do not rush toward any teachings outside the Church, even if the one who speaks them has a name and fame, but stand firm in your Church and its teachings, and by prayer and submission to the guidance of your spiritual fathers, you will discover the error in the teachings of strangers.

Satan stirs people up against one another, so divisions and wars occur, in order that they hate one another, so that he may dominate them and occupy them with problems away from the worship of God, and fill them with anxiety and fear.
"Be not troubled": do not be alarmed by these reports, but expect them, and pray that God may support you and give you peace, and keep those who are within these wars.
"But the end is not yet": these wars remind you to prepare for the end of days, but they are not the final sign before the Day of Judgment.

A second sign that Christ gives is not only divisions and wars, but lack of food and drink, that is, famines, so that many die. Then Satan spreads diseases as epidemics, to frighten people and distract them from God. And he uses another sign, namely earthquakes and all changes in nature, so that people murmur against God.
All these signs will recur many times, but they are the beginning of sorrows, and there are still other signs before the coming of Christ.

Do not be alarmed if afflictions face you, but trust in the power of your God to protect you from the wars of the devil, and to turn the material affliction into growth in your spiritual life; only hold fast to God with prayers and faithfulness in your life.

Besides the general calamities by which the devil tries to make them fall into murmuring, he stirs up afflictions against the children of God in many persecutions for the sake of their faith, so they lose much of the comfort of the body, and are even exposed to torments that reach death; and by this he tries to keep them away from God, and even to deny Christ.

In the face of the persecutions that confront the children of God, some believers fear and doubt, so they apostatize from the faith and resist their brethren, and ally with the wicked to persecute the believers, so they deliver them to wicked rulers to be punished and killed, and by this divisions and hatred occur between those who apostatize from the faith and their believing brethren, and they even become more persecuting of their brethren than the outside persecutors.

Look to your Christ, who endured many sufferings unto death, that you may accept afflictions for His sake. And do not be disturbed if those nearest to you resist you, but stand firm in your love for God and for them, and pray for them that they may return to the faith, confident that God supports you, so that no one harms you except by His permission.

The third blow that Satan directs at the children of God, after the general calamities and the particular afflictions, is to lead them astray from the truth by the appearance of many false prophets, that is, people who claim to be sent by God, or the holders of philosophies and doctrines that draw people away and make them doubt God and the Church, and make them fall into various desires.
By people's departure from God and their falling into many desires, their love for God grows weak, and they become carnal and far from the spiritual life.
On the other side, a few hold fast to the right faith, and reject the pressures of doubt and deception. And whoever remains steadfast declares his faith and his love, and receives eternal salvation.

So that man may be without excuse, God provides the call to the right faith to all mankind, so the preaching reaches everyone before the second coming of Christ, to give the opportunity of salvation to all.
Do not be led after any strange teachings or meetings outside the Church, and be careful in your friendships so as to keep your right faith.

If the Christians notice the siege of Jerusalem, whether those who are in it or in the land of Judea surrounding it, let them flee to the mountains around them so that the Roman soldiers do not destroy them. And indeed, those who remained in Jerusalem were killed by Titus, the Roman commander, in very great numbers.
If a person is on the housetop, let him flee quickly when he sees the Roman soldiers approaching from afar, and not think of his belongings that are in the house, so that he may escape with his life.
Those working in the fields must run swiftly forward, and not return even to take their clothes that they had taken off to do their work.
The difficulty of flight is evident for pregnant women and nursing mothers who carry the unborn and small children, because they are weighed down by what they carry.

Would that this destruction and the flight from it not be in winter, so that the rains would not hinder the flight and the roads would not be muddy, and also not on a Sabbath, so that their conscience would not trouble them that they are running long distances on the Sabbath day against what the Law commands, or so that the Jewish police would not prevent them from that.

And from the spiritual side, all the above signifies fleeing quickly from evil to the mountains, which indicate rising with God above the world, and not descending to desires or falling back to them, and seeking God's help to support our weakness if we are weighed down by the burdens and labors of this world.
Let us hasten to flee, caring for the salvation of our souls before everything, and giving up material things that we may receive the Kingdom.

The attack of Titus the Roman on Jerusalem was violent, and he killed in it more than a million Jews, in addition to those he killed in Judea; there had been no destruction like it in all this region. "Such as was not since the beginning ... no, nor ever shall be": that is, no destruction this cruel had occurred in Jerusalem, and none will occur afterward to this extent.
And this signifies the great tribulation that will occur in the whole world before the Day of Judgment, such as there was not before, nor ever shall be.
God intervened, so the siege of Jerusalem lasted only five months, so that all who were in it would not perish. God did this so that the Christians would flee to the mountains as He had told them.

This also applies to the end of days, when there will be severe persecution from Satan against the children of God so that they turn back from their faith, and he will press them hard even in obtaining the necessities of life, and torture and kill many. But the love of God will make this period short, so that the faith of His children does not weaken and they do not deny their Christ, but He permits afflictions in proportion to the endurance of His children, and gives them help to flee from them, and to take refuge in the Church and spiritual worship, and so find their salvation.

Be reassured, for God does not let you be tempted above your strength, and He supports you in affliction, and even makes it a motive for your drawing near to Him; so trust that the hand of God, the Pantocrator, your heavenly Father, directs your life and nothing harms you.

entries.section: (9) The second coming is announced to all

paragraphs.text: Christ warns His children of the appearance of wicked people who claim to be He, and pretend to piety, but slip in strange teachings to lead the believers astray. So one must keep away from them and reject their teachings as long as they are outside the Church, whatever their miracles, for Satan is able to do miracles, but they are not constructive. And as long as a person is obedient to the Church and her fathers, there is no fear for him of going astray.

entries.section: (9) The second coming is announced to all

paragraphs.text: Part of the deception is the claim that the coming and appearance of Christ will be to a few in some place, such as a certain desert, or hidden in a closed place with a special group; so Christ warns that His coming will be announced to all mankind at the same time.

entries.section: (9) The second coming is announced to all

paragraphs.text: Christ gives a comparison for His coming with the lightning that appears in the sky, which all people see, whether in the east or the west; thus no one needs to warn another of the coming of Christ. It is to be noted that lightning appears suddenly and is clear to all who look, and thus will be the second coming of Christ.

entries.section: (9) The second coming is announced to all

paragraphs.text: This verse can be meant of the destruction of Jerusalem, for the carcase is the Jewish nation that had departed from God, so it became dead to Him, and the Romans fell upon it like eagles and destroyed Jerusalem, and they carried their emblem, which is the eagles, on their standards as they attacked Jerusalem.

This verse also applies to the end of days, when the eagles, who are the angels, swoop upon the wicked, who are signified by the carcase, to declare God's wrath and judgment on them, to cast them into eternal torment. Likewise, the carcase is meant of the crucified Christ, who is given on the altar in His Church every day as true Body and Blood; there the saints gather, who are raised up in a heavenly life like eagles flying in the height of heaven. Thus at the coming of Christ, His children gather around Him by means of the angels, and rejoice with Him. And on the contrary, the wicked gather around the devil in eternal torment.
If you are like the eagle, one of the children of God, your place of gathering is around Christ in the Church, and you will always find your rest and your joy.

Christ continues His talk about the Day of Judgment, for after the collapse of nature, the sign of the Son of man appears in heaven, which is the Cross, with light and glory. Then all the unbelievers and the unrepentant tremble and are put to shame, because they refused to believe in the crucified Christ, and even crucified Him many times in their lives by their immersion in evil, and they mourn in remorse without hope. And He calls them "the tribes of the earth", to distinguish them from the heavenly children of God who believe in Him. Then Christ Himself appears in great glory on the clouds of heaven, because we have become accustomed that the cloud indicates the presence of God, as happened in the days of Moses and at the Transfiguration.
And His appearance in His glory is utterly different from the image of His humility at His first coming in the flesh.

The angels of God appear at once with trumpets of shouting, joy and victory, to gather the children of God who believe in Him from the four corners of the world, to reign forever with their Christ. They gather not only the dwellers of heaven, that is, the spirits of the saints, but all those who lived a heavenly life on earth.
How great and joyful is that day for the children of God! Let us prepare with repentance and great exactness, and endure the sufferings of life that we may be glorified with Him.

entries.section: (12) The parable of the fig tree

paragraphs.text: Christ gives a parable here, namely the fig tree, which appears dry in the winter season, but when summer comes the sap flows in its branches, and it is filled with leaves, blossoms and fruit, and this is evidence of the arrival of the summer season.
Likewise, if the signs previously mentioned in this chapter (vv. 5-15) appear, this means that the destruction of Jerusalem is near.
If evil increases and you endure many afflictions, this means that the relief of the affliction is near, and God's glorifying you.

entries.section: (12) The parable of the fig tree

paragraphs.text: "This generation": a generation includes from 30 to 40 years, and the destruction of Jerusalem occurred forty years after these words, and some of the hearers lived until the destruction of Jerusalem, such as John the Beloved. Christ specifies the time of the fulfilment of these signs, which is the generation in which those who hear Him live, and He means the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70.
He also means the spread of faith in Him in the continents known at that time, and the beginning of the believers' preparation for the eternal Kingdom.

entries.section: (13) The time of the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: Christ affirms the truth of His words and the certainty of their fulfilment, for they are more steadfast than anything known to mankind.

For though the earth is firm under their feet, and the heaven is high above them, they will pass away on the Day of Judgment, so that the word of God may be fulfilled, and He takes His children into His Kingdom. And heaven signifies the spirit that goes to it, and earth the body that is laid in it. That is, people die over the course of generations, but in the end these signs and His second coming must be fulfilled.

entries.section: (13) The time of the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: No one must be occupied with fixing the time of His coming, for He will not announce it even to His angels, so that people do not grow slack in their striving and spiritual preparation, or tremble and fear so that their spiritual movement is paralyzed. Since God will not announce the time of His coming, nor the day of your departure from the world, you must prepare every day with repentance, prayer and love for others.

entries.section: (14) Preparing for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: He gives a comparison for our present life in which we prepare for the coming of Christ, with what happened in the days of Noah. For before the flood, people were occupied with their desires and material affairs, marrying, eating and drinking, forgetting their relationship with God and repentance for their sins. Likewise now in our life, there are many who are occupied with their worldly concerns away from the salvation of their souls.

entries.section: (14) Preparing for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: The flood came suddenly, and because they were not prepared they perished.
Likewise the coming of Christ comes suddenly, and only those prepared by a life of repentance are saved.

entries.section: (14) Preparing for the coming of Christ

paragraphs.text: People will be mingled together in their living in one family or work or neighborhood, but some of them care about preparing for eternity, and the other is absorbed in his desires, refusing repentance. Then the one is taken to the heavenly glories, and the other is left to be cast into eternal torment.

Do not be absorbed in material preoccupations, for they are not the goal of your life, but the goal is the love of God. So accustom yourself to a relationship with Him in prayers, fasts and spiritual readings, so that if the day of the end surprises you, you will be at rest, indeed glorified with joy unspeakable.

entries.section: (15) The parable of the goodman of the house and the thief

paragraphs.text: Christ continues His talk about preparation for the Kingdom, and proclaims openly the importance of spiritual watchfulness, that is, vigilance and attention to the salvation of the soul by repentance, and examining oneself every day, and caring for spiritual practices, that our love for God may grow, and from it result love, forgiveness and service to others. And the reason for His emphasis on the importance of watchfulness, that is, constant preparation, is our not knowing the time of His coming.

entries.section: (15) The parable of the goodman of the house and the thief

paragraphs.text: "Watch": a division of the night, which the Jews divide into four divisions.
"The thief": death, and also a figure of the sudden coming of the Son of man.
"Broken up": robbed.
"In an hour when ye think not": in an hour you do not know.

Christ gives a parable about the importance of spiritual watchfulness to face the thief (death), who comes during the night, seizing the opportunity of the sleep of those in the house to break in and enter from any place to rob it. If the goodman of the house, who is responsible for it, knew the time of the thief's coming, he would stay awake to prevent him from robbing his house.
Then He affirms the importance of preparation, because Christ has not and will not specify the time of His coming.
Be careful lest Satan direct your thought and senses toward evil desires until he persuades you of their necessity, and you are surprised by the Day of Judgment and cannot do anything.

entries.section: (16) The parable of the faithful servant

paragraphs.text: Christ presents another parable of a master who appoints one of his servants as steward for him to care for the needs of those working for him, and travels for a time. Then He asks about the qualities of the faithful and wise servant, and answers that he is the one who gives food to all in the house at the right time.
"The servant": every Christian: a father or mother or servant responsible for shepherding and serving others.
"Faithful": he who fulfils his duties in the fullest way.
"Wise": he who prepares for his eternity by spiritual watchfulness.
"His lord": Christ.
"His household": all the souls surrounding the Christian or servant, whom God requires him to shepherd and care for spiritually.
"Meat": spiritual care, and what it also includes of meeting material and psychological needs. "In due season": that is, at the right time when they need it.

entries.section: (16) The parable of the faithful servant

paragraphs.text: He commends the servant who does what his master charged him with throughout the period of his journey, and rewards him by appointing him steward over all his possessions.

And by this he signifies the importance of each one's care for the salvation of his own soul, and the satisfying of his spirit and body by a living relationship with God, and his caring also for serving all those around him and drawing souls to Christ. And the reward is that He raises him to heaven to give him the knowledge of God, and constant enjoyment of fellowship with Him.
"When his lord cometh": the coming of Christ on the Day of Judgment.
"So doing": continuing in his faithfulness and spiritual vigilance and preparation for eternity.
"Verily": an affirmation of the importance of what He is about to declare.
"All his goods": that is, the knowledge of God in eternity and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (16) The parable of the faithful servant

paragraphs.text: The unfaithful servant behaves in evil after being appointed steward to care for the servants in the house, so instead of caring for their needs, he is harsh to them, thinking that his master will not come soon. And he is absorbed in satisfying his material pleasures, which are represented by eating and drinking wine to drunkenness.

"That evil servant": the Christian or servant who neglects his relationship with God and is occupied with evil desires. "Delayeth his coming": he forgets the preparation for the day of the Lord on the pretext that there is still a long time in life, so he plunges into desires.
"Smite his fellowservants": cruelty and injustice in treating others.
"Eat and drink with the drunken": absorption in pleasures and material desires.

entries.section: (16) The parable of the faithful servant

paragraphs.text: "Lord": a figure of God.
"That servant": the selfish person occupied with his corrupt desires, who has no love toward others, and ignores preparing for his eternity.
"Cut him asunder": that is, destroy him.

The master comes suddenly without appointment, and sees the unfaithfulness of his servant in his service, so he destroys him and casts him with the wicked hypocrites into eternal torment where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, that is, very severe pains and despair, because he pretends to be a steward for God in caring for himself and those around him, while in truth he corrupts himself and wrongs others. Examine the responsibilities and the souls among whom God has placed you, to draw them to Him, and ask yourself how faithful you are with your time and talents and all your abilities, and have you used them for the glory of God or for your personal mood and turned aside with them into evil?
And do you pray and strive for the salvation of every soul around you?
Chapter twenty-five: the parables of the virgins and the talents; the work of mercy
"The kingdom of heaven": that is, God's heavenly reign over the hearts of His children in the Church, in preparation for the eternal Kingdom.
"Ten": a number that signifies completeness, that is, all mankind who believe in God.
"Virgins": they signify the human souls that believe in God.
"Their lamps": they signify the abilities of man, that is, spirit and body, by which he lives with God, so that his life is illumined.
"The bridegroom": he is God.
So all are believers and their goal is eternity, that is, being with the Bridegroom forever. But they differ in how they prepare for the Kingdom.
"Five": this indicates the five senses of man, which he uses either well, like the wise virgins, or hands over to evil, like the foolish.
"Wise": they had the appearance of piety and its depth, which is the oil in the lamps.
"Foolish": these are the ones who had the appearance of the spiritual life, but had no oil, which is the love of God and the service of others.

And foolishness is that a person has the ability to enjoy God and fellowship with Him in this life and forever, and is negligent in this out of laziness and preoccupation with the world and its many concerns.
"Slumbered ... and slept": that is, the end of life and death.
The life of these virgins ended and they died, because the Bridegroom, that is, Christ, had not yet come.

"At midnight": this indicates the second coming of Christ after the repose of souls, and the revealing of His just judgment, where He rewards those who fell asleep in the faith, and recompenses those whom the darkness of the wicked world swallowed up. "A cry": the voices of the angels with the last trumpet calling the believers to salvation, and the wicked to judgment. "Go ye out to meet him": the bodies of the departed are changed, and gathered after their decomposition, and become spiritual bodies united with their spirits, to meet Christ and stand before Him on the Day of Judgment.
At the second coming of Christ, the bodies rise, and all mankind gathers on the Day of Judgment.

All the virgins came forward, that is, all mankind, to stand before God the just Judge. And each one gathered what he had of faith and love, that is, trimmed his lamp, and stood to be judged before God.

And only here the foolish realized that faith without love, that is, the oil, is of no benefit and the lamp goes out, because faith without works is dead; the demons believe and tremble, but they will not be saved. The foolish virgins tried to take oil from the wise, but they excused themselves because it would not suffice for them and for the foolish, and they should look for this oil and buy it from the sellers, that is, offer love and mercy to others, because good works, however much a person does, do not exceed and overflow beyond him so that he can give them to others. And Christ's saying is clear: "So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do" (Lk 17:10).
"Them that sell": that is, every person with whom we can do a work of mercy, such as the poor and needy.

The foolish virgins tried to show mercy and do good on the Day of Judgment, but there was no longer any opportunity. For Christ took the wise virgins and went in with them to the Kingdom, and the door was shut, and there was no longer any opportunity for anyone to enter after that.
"The marriage": the eternal Kingdom.

"The door was shut": this means the guarantee of the wise virgins' permanence in the Kingdom, and the preventing of the wicked and Satan from entering, so that the righteous face no troubles in the Kingdom.
And on the other hand, there is no opportunity at all for the wicked to escape eternal torment far from God.
"Afterward": that is, after it was too late and they were sentenced to judgment.
"Open to us": they ask for a place in the Kingdom.
"I know you not": He does not know them as disciples and followers of His.

The foolish virgins tried to enter after the door was shut, but Christ refused, and even declared that He did not know them, that is, He has no relationship with them, because they had the appearance of piety and not its power and depth, that is, faith without works of love.
Whoever does not live in the love of God on earth has no place to enjoy His love in heaven.
Christ comments plainly, affirming the importance of spiritual watchfulness, that is, constant preparation for His coming, because we do not know its time.

God awaits your practical love in care for your holy worship of Him, and good works with everyone you meet. So seize the opportunity of your life to do good as far as you are able, and your life on earth will be illumined, and you will not be put to shame on the Day of Judgment.
"Travelling": by Christ's ascension to heaven, He left mankind for the length of their lives, to strive in their spiritual life on earth until His second coming.
"His goods": all the abilities of mankind are divine gifts with which they are entrusted as stewards for God, and they will give an account for them on the last day.

"According to his several ability": all the abilities that he can use, for God did not withhold His gifts from anyone, and did not give him abilities greater than his capacity, lest he be confused by them or show his inability.
"Took his journey": He left mankind in their freedom to invest their abilities throughout their lives.
God likened Himself to a man and mankind to His servants, and gave them talents, that is, money, to trade with and invest, and travelled for an unknown time.

And God's gifts and endowments differ from one person to another, for some receive more than others, and God will judge each one according to what he received, so let not him who received more be proud, and let not him who received less envy or be jealous; what matters is faithfulness in investing the abilities of mankind that God has given them, many or few.

The one who had five talents traded, signifying one who invested his five senses, and gained five other talents, that is, he came to have the inner senses, which are the ability to know God, and not only knowledge of the material world around him, that is, he came to have the inner eye, which is insight, and the inner ear, that is, hearing the voice of God... and so on.

As for the one who had two talents, and the number two signifies love, like the bridegroom and his bride, when he traded with his two talents, he also gained two other talents, that is, his love was doubled, so it became for God and also for all mankind.

The last servant, who had one talent, signifies the selfish person, that is, he loves himself only, for he is lazy and did not weary himself by offering love to God and to others, but hid his talent in the earth, that is, he was immersed in earthly desires and luxuriated in pleasures to satisfy his personal mood, forgetting that he is a steward over this talent, which is God's property.
Each of us is a steward over his life, because it is the property of God who bought us with His blood. So we must live for Him, faithful in investing all our abilities and gifts.
"After a long time": this is the long opportunity of life that God gave to every person, so that he may invest his abilities for the glory of His holy name.
After this life ends, the Day of Judgment comes, that is, the master comes to reckon with his servants.

The one who had five talents presented what he had gained, which was five other talents, and his master commended him and described him as good, because he lived for God and the love of others, and also faithful because he invested all his energies and achieved a profit of 100%. And he rewarded him for his faithfulness on earth, which is the little, by granting him life in the Kingdom where He gives him great blessings, which are expressed by the much, that is, he lives in love like a bride with her bridegroom forever in constant joy with God, his master and heavenly Father.
And it is understood from this that each one will be judged for himself, and for every divine gift given to him to invest, because he is a steward over it.
"Well": that is, rightly, and it is a praise from God than which there is none greater.

The second servant presented the two talents that he had gained like the first servant, and his master commended him like the first, in the same measure and with the same qualities, that he was good and faithful, and gave him the same reward, which is entering the Kingdom, because he achieved a complete profit, which is 100%.

The third servant was selfish and wicked, because he fell into negligence, and slipped into other sins, not only neglect and not using his abilities for God's account, that is, love of God and others, but, instead of loving others, he began to wrong them and also his master, that is, God, and described him as hard and greedy, taking though he had not given, and this is the opposite of the truth. But the sin that begins small with laziness and negligence leads to graver sins, and in the end causes the sinner to lose his spiritual insight.
His lying also appears when he says "I was afraid", though he did not fear God and strive spiritually, but was immersed in his earthly desires.
"Thou wicked and slothful servant": the master exposed the true reason for his not trading with the talent, which is his laziness and wickedness.

The master condemned this servant from the words of his mouth, for he said to him: if I am hard and greedy, it would have been better for you to trade with the talent, that is, to use it in material dealings to acquire a profit, and by that He means investing his abilities in the love of God and others.

"The exchangers": where money is used in trade to make a profit, and what is meant is offering love to others. And the exchangers are the specialists in financial dealings, so they signify the fathers and spiritual guides, for when one who walks spiritually obeys them, they guide him how to invest his abilities for the glory of God.
"Usury": the gain that comes from trade, and its meaning here is winning souls for Christ by doing good.

God's punishment of him was first to strip him of his abilities, and then to give them to the one who had come to have ten talents, affirming that everyone who has faithfulness and the love of God is given by God increasing gifts. But as for him who has no love of God and others and is unfaithful, God takes away his gifts from him because he does not deserve them.

The idle (wicked) servant is punished by being cast into eternal torment, expressed by the outer darkness far from God, where there is intense sorrow and violent pain signified by weeping and gnashing of teeth. Be faithful in using your abilities and God's blessings on you will increase, and do not neglect any grace or time available to you (a talent), lest God deprive you of your eternal inheritance.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: After Christ spoke of His second coming in a symbolic way as a bridegroom of the soul or as a master of his servants, He speaks here plainly about the Day of Judgment on which He comes as Judge in great glory, different from the image of weakness in which He lived in the body on earth from His birth in the manger until He was crucified on the Cross. He will come with His angels and sit on the throne of His glory, that is, His throne, to judge the whole world for their deeds in every place and time, and He separates mankind by means of His angels into the righteous, whom He sets on His right hand, for the right hand signifies blessing and strength, while the wicked He sets on His left, a sign of shame and disgrace.

And the distinction will be very easy for God, as the shepherd distinguishes the flock he tends, whether sheep or goats. And the sheep are more obedient and peaceable and submissive to the shepherd than the goats.

And it is clear from Christ's words that in the end there are only two groups, the righteous and the wicked, and He calls them the wise and the foolish, or the faithful servants and the unfaithful, and here He calls them the sheep and the goats. And there is no third place, as some claim, for torturing and punishing the wicked temporarily and then joining them to the righteous.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: Christ the King describes the believers as blessed, and as children of God, His Father and their Father, that is, He declares His fellowship with them in love, and that He is the firstborn among many brethren, so He calls them "blessed of my Father", and welcomes them to inherit His Kingdom, which He prepared for them before they were created, to enjoy with Him in it forever.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: Christ enumerates the works of mercy that the righteous performed, and for which they deserved the inheritance of the Kingdom of Heaven, ascribing the work of mercy to Himself, so He mentions their feeding the hungry and thirsty, materially or spiritually, and their care for strangers, so that they host them, and this care not only meets their needs, but reassures them psychologically to continue life in the new place.
If you meet a stranger anywhere, welcome him and make him feel at home, and open the way for all so that they may be satisfied with Christ, our true food.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: He also mentions clothing the naked, whether with garments or with the righteousness of Christ by walking in virtue. And in sickness, a person feels his weakness, and is moved by the love of those who ask after him, and it is a suitable opportunity to speak to him about God.

And among the hardest cases also are those imprisoned, who have lost their freedom and the ability to go to their loved ones, so when their loved ones come to them they rejoice greatly, and we offer them Christ who never leaves them, even if they are far from people in prison.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: Christ makes clear how the work of mercy is directed to Him personally, so He sets up a gentle dialogue between the righteous and Himself, and they ask Him humbly: when saw we thee, Lord, an hungered or thirsty or sick... and so on, because they feel that they are not worthy of this praise. And He answers them that all that they did of works of mercy with the weak, the poor, the sick or the imprisoned was offered to Him personally. And this is a great divine appreciation of the work of mercy, and indeed a declaration that it is the summit of love and our way to inheriting the Kingdom.
"The least": that is, the needy and the weak.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: Christ calls the wicked on His left, and describes them as deserving the divine curse and eternal torment, though they should have been in the Kingdom that He prepared for them, but they refused to respond to His love. So He casts them now far from Him, and deprives them of His love, which they refused, and they will be forever in the torment of the fire prepared for the devil and his fallen angels, who are the demons, that is, they now become like the demons because they refused the love of God.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: Christ declares the reason for their going to eternal torment, which is their selfishness, and their refusing to feel for others and help them in their various needs.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: The wicked ask when they saw God in need and did not give to Him, so He declares to them that He was in the form of the needy and of those small in their standing and abilities, and they refused to show mercy to them.

entries.section: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

paragraphs.text: Christ affirms that the Day of Judgment is the end, for the righteous continue in the enjoyment of the eternal Kingdom, while the wicked are tormented forever also.
This is your opportunity now for repentance and feeling for others and doing mercy with all who are around you and all whom you meet, before the dreadful Day of Judgment comes.
The Passover; the Lord's Supper; the arrest of Christ and His trial

entries.section: (3) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: Christ came to Bethany (ch. 21:17) for the last time in His life on earth, and entered the house of a man called Simon, who was known as "the leper"; perhaps Christ had healed him of his leprosy, so he was eager to ask Him to visit him in his house.

And a woman came who loved Christ and wanted to express her love for Him, so she bought a bottle of costly perfume and poured it on His head. This woman is Mary the sister of Lazarus, as John the Evangelist mentioned (Jn 12:3), because she was known for her love of Christ, and lived in the same village, and was eager to hear His word. Matthew and Mark the Evangelists did not mention her name out of fear for her from the persecution of the Jews, whereas John wrote his Gospel a long time after the destruction of Jerusalem, when there was no longer any fear of them.

This woman wanted to express her love for Christ, for she represents the Church thankful to her Christ for His gifts and miracles and His care for her. And she declares the existence of a few believers whose hearts were filled with love in the midst of many wicked people who would cry out a few days later for His crucifixion.

"An alabaster box of very precious ointment": a small precious vessel in which costly perfumes are put, with a long neck whose mouth is sealed with a firm material, so it cannot be opened except by breaking this neck.

"On his head": the custom was to pour perfume on the head to honor beloved persons and those of high standing, and Mark also mentioned that (Mk 14:3). (As for John, he mentioned that she poured it on His feet as a sign of her humility) (and it is understood implicitly that she poured part of it on His head as was the custom).

"As he sat at meat": the custom at banquets was to sit on a couch and not a chair, leaning on the left arm on the table, while the legs stretched out on the couch and the feet pointed backward, and one ate with the right hand while leaning with his head on his left hand, and this enabled Mary to reach His head easily.

Mark, like Matthew, mentioned this event without concern for the chronological order of events, whereas John mentioned it at its time, which is six days before the Passover (Jn 12:1), that is, before Christ entered the week of His passion for the salvation of mankind, whose love for Him appeared in the person of Mary, before He endured the sufferings from the multitudes in Jerusalem. As for Matthew and Mark, they mentioned the event two days before the Passover, when Judas Iscariot took counsel to betray Christ to the Jews, to declare that if the disciple had betrayed, there are among men those who love Christ like Mary. And this event is different from the event of the sinful woman's pouring out ointment during Christ's preaching in Galilee, which took place in the house of a Pharisee also called Simon, and St. Luke mentioned it (Lk 7:37-38). Seize today as an opportunity to offer your love to Christ in prayers and hymns, for this may be the last opportunity in your life.

entries.section: (3) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: The disciples and all who were gathered in Simon's house saw this great love offered to Christ, and instead of feeling their shortcoming in offering love to Him like Mary, they began to blame her. The truth is that the one who declared this blame was Judas Iscariot and not the disciples, because he had the bag and was a thief (Jn 12:4-6), and by his words he stirred up the rest of the disciples and likewise those gathered in the house, so they considered her love unwise, even a waste, since in their view it would have been better for this ointment to be sold for much, and (the price) given to the poor, rather than poured on Christ.

And thus they cover their shortcoming in offering love with arguments that seem logical, namely concern for the poor, though the purpose was evil, because Judas wanted the money to be put into the bag so that he could steal a large part of it. "Much": Mark (Mk 14:5) and John (Jn 12:5) mention the price, which is estimated at three hundred denarii, a very large sum.
Do not blame those who spend a long time in prayer, or visiting holy places, or in spiritual retreats, but on the contrary, imitate them, for it is a message to you to offer love like theirs to God.

entries.section: (3) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: Mary was silent, but Christ defended her, affirming the greatness of her love, and He did not reject offering love to the poor as He had taught them in the previous chapter, but the poor are always present, while He, His days on earth were about to end.

And we notice the tenderness of Christ's feelings, that although He knew the evil of Judas, and that the motive for his words was love of money and not love of the poor, He did not blame him or rebuke those present, but praised Mary, and confirmed them in offering love to the poor throughout their lives. And He left an opportunity for Judas to repent and be ashamed of his hidden evil, but he, sadly, did not care, and was determined to betray Christ and sell Him to the Jews.

entries.section: (3) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: Then He added a second praise for the woman, which is that this love of hers is ointment poured on His body that would die on the Cross, so it is like perfumes for the burial of the body, affirming the importance of offering love. The custom among the Jews was to put ointments on the bodies of the departed, to honor them, and this custom still exists among many peoples.

entries.section: (3) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: Christ adds that this great love will be written in the Gospel which will be preached in the whole world, as teaching for all His children of the importance of offering pure love to Him as thanks and response to His love; and this shows the divinity of Christ, who knew that the Gospel would spread in the whole world, and that this event would be written in it. Trust that your love which you offer to Christ will be declared before all mankind on the Day of Judgment, and will remain declared forever. Let this be an encouragement to offer continual worship to God, and to do mercy with every needy person, whatever effort and money it costs you.

"The first day of the feast of unleavened bread": "first" according to the Greek translation is "proto", that is, before, and it is the same word mentioned in (Jn 1:15), when John the Baptist spoke of Christ that He was before him. The meaning of this is that Christ kept the Passover a day before the Jewish Passover, which is called "the feast of the Passover" or "the feast of unleavened bread", because unleavened bread is eaten with the Passover according to the Law (Ex 12:8, 11). And at the same time that the Jews were offering their Passover, Christ was being crucified, because He is the true Passover, signified by the slaughtered lamb that the Jews offer.

The feast of the Passover drew near, and every Jew kept the Passover inside his house with his family. But it is clear from the disciples' question to Christ about the place He chose to keep the Passover in that He had no house of His own. And Christ presented a new concept of the family, not only those bound bodily, but those bound spiritually. So the twelve gathered, and with them Christ, the head of the family, or the head of the body which is the Church. He sent them to a certain person, who tradition says was Mark the Apostle, where He kept the Passover in his house, and the household prepared the Passover with the disciples according to the Jewish Law, and it is a type of the crucified Christ who would offer Himself for the whole world the next day, that is, Great Friday.
"My time is at hand": that is, the time of His passion and crucifixion, which would be accomplished after a day, has drawn near.
"Made ready the passover": the slaughtered lamb and the bitter herbs, and the dishes and cups of wine... and so on, of what the Passover requires according to the Law.
"Even": from the third hour to the fifth hour in the evening, which is the time for eating the Passover according to the Law (Ex 12:6).

While Christ was eating the Passover with His disciples, among them Judas Iscariot the traitor who would betray Him to the Jews, Jesus bore a father's heart toward him, concerned for his salvation, and gently said to His disciples that one of them would betray Him to the Jews, and did not mention his name, in case his heart would be pricked and he would repent.
And on Thursday a group of events took place, namely:
(1) Preparing the Passover.
(2) A dispute among the disciples about which of them was the greatest (Lk 22:24).
(3) Eating the Passover.
(4) Washing the disciples' feet during the eating of the Passover.
(5) Christ's announcement that one of His disciples would betray Him.
(6) The Lord's Supper and the institution of the sacrament of the Eucharist.
(7) Christ tells His disciples that they will leave Him and that Peter will deny Him.
(8) Christ's farewell discourse and His prayer, mentioned in (Jn 14-17).
(9) The singing of the hymn and the departure from the city.
(10) Christ's prayer in Gethsemane.
(11) The arrest of Christ.
God sends you many warnings and messages gently, that perhaps you may repent. So do not neglect His tender love, lest you lose your life far from Him like Judas.

The disciples were moved by the news that one of them would betray Him, and so that Christ would not leave them doubting themselves, He gave a sign of the one who would betray Him, and also to warn Judas a second time that perhaps he would repent. The sign was that the traitor would put his hand into the dish in which Christ was eating and eat from it. But sadly Judas did not take heed and ate from the dish. And from the grief of the disciples, they did not notice this sign, so they did not speak to Judas.

And it was the custom of the Jews that the master of the banquet gives the morsel to the important person sitting at the table, so the sign was an honor and love toward Judas from Christ, that perhaps it would shame him and prick his heart so that he would repent of his evil, for Judas put his hand into Christ's dish, and Christ put out His hand and gave him the morsel.
And it is clear that the morsel was from the Passover meal, and after it Judas went out and did not eat of the Lord's Supper.

Christ warned Judas for the third time, declaring woe to this traitor, for his eternal torment would be severe, indeed it would have been good for him if he had not been born, so as not to commit this great betrayal. And Christ made clear that He must be delivered to the Jews and die by His own will through one of His beloved ones who betrays Him (Ps 41:9), so that His disciples may be reassured that He does this for their salvation and the salvation of all mankind, but here He only warns Judas and gives him an opportunity to repent and review himself.

Judas dared (not out of repentance but out of hypocrisy) and asked Christ: "Master, is it I?" (the one who betrays You). Christ answered him, as a fourth warning to him: "Thou hast said." This is a Jewish expression meaning agreement. And Judas did not take heed, because love of money had blinded his eyes, and the disciples likewise did not take heed and understand, because of their astonishment that one of them would be His betrayer, and their immersion in grief over what would happen to their Teacher. Hasten today to repentance and confession while you have the opportunity, before a day comes on which you lose your sense of repentance, however many divine warnings you are given.

After Christ finished eating the Passover with His disciples, He instituted the sacrament of thanksgiving, that is, He gave them His most holy Body and Blood, for He took bread and blessed it and changed it into His Body, and gave it to them to eat, declaring that this is His true Body. And likewise the cup, He changed the wine in it into His Blood, declaring that it would be shed for all mankind on the Cross.

And thus He gave His Church the greatest of the sacraments, the sacrament of Communion, that we may be united with Him throughout the ages, so that we do not only see Christ as the people of His time saw Him, but touch Him and He enters into us, and unites with us, so that He lives in us and we in Him, and we also are united with one another by each of us partaking of His Body and Blood, so we all become members of His body which is the Church.
"And as they were eating": that is, immediately after they finished eating the Passover, He instituted the sacrament of the Eucharist (thanksgiving), because the Passover is a type of it.

"Bread": it is leavened bread, because we are a day before the Passover. Therefore the Church offers on the altar leavened bread and not unleavened, because Christ bore our sins, which the leaven indicates, and died on the Cross, and so wiped away every punishment from us.

"The disciples": they represent the whole Church of the New Testament, and therefore in the rite of the Liturgy, the priest divides the Body of Christ into 12 parts representing the twelve disciples around the middle part called the Lordly part, that is, the Spadikon, that is, Christ in the midst of His people, or Christ the head of the Church.
"My blood": which the blood of animals in the Old Testament signifies, and without shedding of blood is no remission (Heb 9:22).
"The new testament": blood was used anciently to confirm covenants by the shedding of the blood of animals, as happened with Abraham (Gen 15:9-19).
"Many": a declaration that Christ's redemption is for the whole world, and everyone who believes in Him and partakes of this Blood receives salvation from his sins.
"For the remission of sins": an affirmation that the sacrament of thanksgiving forgives sins, sharing in this with the sacrament of repentance and confession.

Christ declares a new truth to His disciples and to all who believe in Him, which is that He will not perform the sacrament of thanksgiving again on earth, that is, He will not change the fruit of the vine, which is the wine, into His Blood, until He drinks it with His children in the eternal Kingdom, but in a new form suited to their existence in the Spirit, that is, our love and union and growth in the knowledge of Christ extend into the eternal Kingdom, not by partaking of bread and wine that change into His Body and Blood, but we are united with Him in a spiritual way suited to our spiritual state in heaven.
"That day": a day of gathering with you in the eternal Kingdom.

"Sung an hymn": the Jews were accustomed to sing Psalms 115 and 116 at the end of their eating of the Passover. And after their singing, Christ spoke to them a long talk, and then prayed His intercessory prayer (Jn 14-17). They offered prayers and hymns fitting for the sacrament of thanksgiving, as happens in the Divine Liturgy during the distribution of the Holy Mysteries, and He went out with them to the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem, where He used to spend periods of quiet retreat with them, to bid them His last farewell before He died.

Christ was not content with sermons and counsels for you, but gives you the power to carry them out, which is His Body and Blood that you partake of and that unite with you, and so work in you to carry out His word, and the hardest commandments become easy by His power. So take care to partake regularly of the Holy Mysteries, because they are the greatest power in the world that keeps you from the wars of the devil and makes you grow in the knowledge of God every day.

As Christ was walking with His disciples to the Mount of Olives, He told them a bitter truth, which is their doubting Him that He is the Christ the Savior, since they were still thinking of Him as an earthly king, so when they see Him arrested, they doubt Him. And this is a fulfilment of the prophecies of the Old Testament, that Satan will smite the Shepherd by arresting Him and crucifying Him, and His flock will be scattered (Zech 13:7).
But when Satan smote Christ by His crucifixion, Christ turned this blow upon Satan, so He bound him with His Cross, and gathered all His children to save and redeem them.
"The Shepherd": He is Christ.
"The flock": they are the disciples of Christ.

Despite the bitter truth, which is the doubt of Christ's disciples nearest to Him concerning Him, He will accomplish their salvation on the Cross, and die, and rise from the dead, and appear to them in Galilee where He was accustomed to walk with them in the fields from city to city. So He encourages them again that He will rise, but sadly they did not take in His words; and Christ repeated that He would appear to them in Galilee at His appearing after His resurrection to the Magdalene (ch. 28:10, 7).

The tender God loves you despite the weakness of your faith, and encourages you by His word and His gifts. So stand firm during the affliction, confident that He will support you and appear clearly in your life.

Peter rushed forward with human emotion, declaring his faith in Christ and his steadfastness in Him whatever the circumstances, even if everyone doubted Him. So Christ made clear to him that, because of his weakness, he would not endure facing the difficult situation, which is His being arrested to be killed. And then, that is, on this night, before the cock crows, he would deny Him, not only once, but three times, as confirmation of his human weakness.
Peter's words show his love for Christ, but at the same time show his mistake in rashness and pride, in feeling that he was better than others in the steadfastness of his faith.

Peter affirmed his clinging to Christ even unto death, and likewise all the disciples. And Christ did not answer them, so that they might see for themselves the extent of their weakness, for in the hour of affliction, at His arrest, all forsook Him and fled (v. 56).
Ask for the help of the Holy Spirit, and He will support you at the time of affliction so that you hold fast to your faith, for it is hard for you to face affliction alone.
"A place": a field or a place with crops, and it seems that its owner knew Christ, so He was accustomed to go there with His disciples.
"Here": probably at the entrance of the garden.
"The disciples": He means the eight disciples, because Judas had left them. And the three, Peter, James and John, would enter with Him into the garden.
"Even unto death": intense sorrow can lead to death, so He expresses the severity of the sorrows He feels.

Christ arrived with His disciples at the Mount of Olives in a garden where it seems He was accustomed to retreat with them, and it is called the garden of Gethsemane, which means "oil press", and it is near Jerusalem, and He left His disciples to retire or pray, and the three nearest to Him advanced with Him, Peter and James and John the sons of Zebedee, to pray apart, for these three had spiritual stature, so He could reveal to them what was in His soul, and He said to them: "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death".

And this sorrow was because He, the Righteous One, would bear the sins of the whole world, for how can righteousness agree with sin?! How painful that is to soul and spirit, in addition to His grief for the Jews who would reject Him and crucify Him while He seeks their salvation.
And He asked His three disciples to pray, indeed to continue in prayer with watchfulness and vigilance.

The disciples were moved, though they did not understand exactly all the dimensions of this sorrow, because the Holy Spirit had not yet descended upon them for them to understand the salvation offered to them.

This confirms the humanity of Christ, for He needed psychologically His close friends, the disciples, to pray with Him in the garden, and the three disciples especially to be nearer to Him in the depth of the garden.

After that, He left the three disciples and advanced alone to pray, and He withdrew from His disciples so as not to disturb them if they saw the intensity of His sorrow. And He felt the difficulty of the cup of suffering, not only the bodily in the crucifixion and death, but rather the psychological when everyone would leave Him, and even more the spiritual by bearing the sins of the world while He is the Righteous and Holy One. And this is a confirmation of His humanity that suffers bodily and psychologically, and in order to show the extent of His obedience and submission to the will of the divinity in Him, so He speaks with the Father, saying: "not my will, but thine, be done".

"Fell on his face": and here, He teaches us the rite of prayer and prostrations (metanoias), that is, bowing down and humbling ourselves before God in afflictions, that He may support us by His grace.
"O my Father": a declaration of the importance of feeling God's fatherhood in prayer, so that it may support us in our afflictions. "The cup": the sufferings He would meet.

It is your right to cry out to God in all your afflictions, and ask for what you need, but quickly follow it with the prayer "thy will be done", and you surrender your life to Him, and leave Him, the tender Father, to choose for you what suits you, and support you in your afflictions.
"The disciples": that is, the three, Peter, James and John.
"One hour": a short period, and not precisely a clock hour.

After He prayed alone, He returned to His three disciples, and found them asleep from weariness and sorrow, so He woke them to pray after gently rebuking them for their sleeping, directing His words to Peter: "What, could ye not watch with me one hour?"

And He declared the importance of prayer with spiritual vigilance, so that the devil does not make us fall into temptations and sins. And He also affirmed that the spirit, if it is active and cares for prayer, can support the weak body that inclines to laziness and rest. So He gently encourages them that their spirits can be active, and so support their body that is weak from weariness and sorrow.
Complete your prayers and readings at night however exhausted you are, for God rejoices in your love however weak your concentration in them.

Christ returned to pray alone with the same words, and came back to His disciples and found them asleep a second time. And this confirms that in the hour of affliction they were not able to stand with Him; and how this increased His sorrows. But He did not weary, but went a third time to pray to the same effect.

Persevere in your prayers and your relationship with God, and hold fast to your principles however much those around you abandon you or even resist you, for Christ teaches you the importance of persistence in prayer, especially in times of affliction.

When He returned to them, He rebuked them with disapproval for the third time, not only the three but all the disciples, saying: "Sleep on now, and take your rest". So they began to take heed; then He told them that the hour of His arrest and the beginning of His entering into the sufferings of the crucifixion had come, and called them to wake up quickly, because Judas who would betray Him to the Jews had drawn near with the Temple guards to arrest Him.

It is to be noted that these Temple guards were Jews and not Romans; they were a body of guards appointed by the priests to maintain the order of the Temple, since the Law did not permit Roman soldiers to enter the Temple lest it be defiled.
"One of the twelve": to show his betrayal, since he was one of the close ones, so how could he betray his Master?!

"A great multitude": includes the Jewish Temple guards and the Roman soldiers assigned to guard the Temple from outside, and the soldiers of the high priest, and some of the followers of the priests who resist Christ.
"Great": a large number came to ensure the arrest of Christ, lest His disciples and those who love Him resist that. "The elders of the people": some members of the Sanhedrin.

"Kissed him": Judas used the expression of love, which is the kiss, in hypocrisy, to carry out his betrayal by the arrest of Christ. While Christ was waking His disciples, His disciple Judas Iscariot came with a great number of soldiers armed with swords and staves, and gave greeting to Christ and kissed Him, and this was the agreed sign, that is, to arrest the one he kisses, and that was for certainty, for Christ was known to the multitudes, but so that the men of the chief priests and the elders of the people would not err and arrest another who resembled Him.

Christ rebuked Judas and warned him, for perhaps he would repent, asking him: "Friend, wherefore art thou come?" Perhaps he would be ashamed of what he was doing (which is betraying Christ and delivering Him to the Jews), but sadly he continued in his evil, and commanded the crowd with him, and they arrested Christ.
Do not make light of the successive opportunities for repentance that God allows you, so that you do not have the fate of Judas in the end.

"One": he is Peter (Jn 18:10-11), and Matthew did not mention him out of fear for him from the persecution of the Jews, whereas John mentioned him because he wrote his Gospel after the destruction of Jerusalem, and there was no longer any fear after the breaking of the power of the Jews.
"Smote off his ear": Peter was a fisherman and had no experience in using the sword, so he could only strike the ear of this servant and cut it off.
"His place": that is, its sheath (its scabbard).

Peter was disturbed when he saw his Teacher and beloved arrested, so he rushed and took a sword, because the disciples had two swords as mentioned in (Lk 22:38). And in an attempt to defend Christ, he cut off the ear of the high priest's servant, named Malchus (Jn 18:10), but Christ commanded him to return his sword to its sheath, and declared that whoever lives by violence will suffer from violence.

And Christ wanted to remove evil from the heart of Peter and all His disciples toward those who are hostile to them, for He came to establish love in the hearts of His children even toward enemies, and to affirm that love is stronger than violence. And by His death that was about to be accomplished, He was able to trample death, and save His children from their sins, and bind the devil, and then rise victorious, declaring the victory and power of love.
"Thinkest thou": meaning: do you doubt my power after you have seen my many miracles?
"Twelve legions of angels": that is, instead of the twelve weak disciples.

Christ warned Peter and all the disciples of His great power, for the hosts of heaven are all under His obedience, that is, the angels, each of whom has power greater than all mankind, and He can ask for more than twelve legions of them, and He means a very abundant number. But by His will He surrenders Himself and dies to save His children, as the prophecies were written about Him in the Old Testament, such as (Isa 53:7).

Christ also rebuked the crowd for coming out by night with swords and staves to arrest Him, as though they were arresting a fugitive thief, though He had been with them every day teaching in the Temple in the midst of the multitudes, and that was to show their deceit and weakness, for they came to arrest Him away from the multitudes so that no one would resist them; and perhaps by this rebuke He wanted to give them an opportunity to repent also.
"Daily": that is, many days, in which He taught openly in the Temple.
"I sat": that is, I taught quietly, and did not make a disturbance, as criminals do.
"Teaching in the temple": that is, openly and clearly before all, so there was no need for you to come by night as though I were a fugitive from justice.
"Ye laid no hold on me": because you have no charges against me, and because of your fear of the people who regard me as a great teacher.

Christ affirmed that what they were doing was the fulfilment of the prophecies of the prophets, and when they arrested Him, all the disciples were afraid and fled, so as not to be arrested, for their refuge and strength were lost, since they had thought that He would protect them from the violence of the Romans and the Jews (Isa 63:3, 5). And of course, their leaving Christ caused Him psychological pain, because of their retreating from their promises not to leave Him even unto death. But in His love, He found an excuse for them, and forgave them their weakness after His resurrection.
Do not be alarmed if your loved ones leave you in the hour of affliction, for God will not leave you. And do not be angry with them, but find an excuse for them, which is human weakness.
Jesus was led to the palace of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders were gathered in preparation for His trial (see the commentary on v. 66).
